definition_en: a unit of distance equal to one thousand metres, used for roads, journeys, and maps
core_image: 公路边一块写着距某城若干公里的白色路牌
scene: 黄昏的省道上，路边立着指示里程的白牌。 The sign said the next town was eight kilometres away, so we kept walking.
sceneCN: 这里 kilometre 是「千米、公里」（第 1 个义项：距离单位，等于一千米），句意是牌子上说下一个镇还有八公里，于是他们继续走。画面里有黄昏、省道和白色路牌。

pos.zh: 千米（口语中作为一整段距离）

derivatives.zh: 截短形式，口语里也可泛指「一公里」或「一公斤」
kilometre 的基本单位，源自希腊语的「量度」
kilometre 加 -ic 构成的形容词，指以公里计的，多用于书面
与 kilometre 同一义场的里程计算说法，由 mile 加 -age 构成

senses.title: A unit of distance of a thousand metres
senses.definition: a metric unit of length equal to one thousand metres
senses.definitionCN: 公制长度单位，等于一千米
senses.example: The lake is three kilometres across.
senses.exampleCN: 这个湖宽三公里。
senses.why: The name is a compound of thousand and metre, so the unit explains its own size.
senses.whyCN: 名字本身就是「千」加「米」的复合，单位自己在解释大小。

senses.title: Distance written on signs and maps
senses.definition: the unit used to state the distance between places
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明两地之间距离的单位
senses.example: Every kilometre is marked on the map.
senses.exampleCN: 地图上每一公里都标了出来。
senses.why: The word takes on a mapping sense because roads and charts must state distances in one shared unit.
senses.whyCN: 公路和地图必须用同一个单位写明距离，于是这个词带上了制图意义。

senses.title: A measure of speed
senses.definition: the unit in which speed is stated as kilometres per hour
senses.definitionCN: 以每小时公里数表示速度时的单位
senses.example: The limit here is fifty kilometres an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的限速是每小时五十公里。
senses.why: Speed is distance over time, so a distance unit naturally appears in every speed limit.
senses.whyCN: 速度是距离除以时间，所以每个限速牌上都自然出现距离单位。

senses.title: A measure of area
senses.definition: the unit squared, used for land and large surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 平方之后用来量土地和大面积
senses.example: The park covers forty square kilometres.
senses.exampleCN: 这座公园占地四十平方公里。
senses.why: Once a length unit exists, squaring it gives the unit for land, and the word simply doubles up.
senses.whyCN: 长度单位一确立，平方一下就得到土地单位的说法，这个词只是叠加使用。

senses.title: A stretch of distance in speech
senses.definition: a loose way of naming a short distance, as in the last kilometre of a race
senses.definitionCN: 口语里指一小段路程，如赛跑的最后一段
senses.example: He pulled ahead in the final kilometre.
senses.exampleCN: 他在最后一公里拉开了距离。
senses.why: Once the word means a stretch of road, the last stretch of a race can be named in it without any measuring.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指一段路，赛跑的最后一段就可以用它来称呼，而不必真的去量。

intro.en: Kilometre is a French-built modern word: a Greek prefix for thousand joined to a French unit of length.
intro.cn: kilometre 是法国人造的现代词：希腊语表示「千」的前缀接上法语长度单位。

items.en: The prefix comes from khilioi, Greek for a thousand.
items.cn: 前缀来自希腊语 khilioi，意为一千。

items.en: The base comes from metron, meaning measure.
items.cn: 词基本自 metron，意为「量度」。

items.en: French scientists coined metre as a unit of length in the late eighteenth century.
items.cn: 十八世纪末法国科学家造出 metre 作为长度单位。

items.en: Kilometre was formed on the same pattern for a thousand metres.
items.cn: kilometre 按同一模式造成，指一千米。

items.en: English took the word in the nineteenth century and later shortened the ending to kilometer in American use.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪引入，美国后来把词尾缩成 kilometer。

note.en: The look-alike group holds units built with the same Greek prefix; the near-meaning group holds older and non-metric measures of distance.
note.cn: 形近组收用同一希腊前缀构成的单位；近义组收更早的和非公制的距离单位。

entries.definition: A thousand grams, the same pattern applied to mass.
entries.definitionCN: 一千克，同一模式用在质量上。

entries.definition: A thousand watts, the same pattern applied to power.
entries.definitionCN: 一千瓦，同一模式用在功率上。

entries.definition: The unit to which the prefix thousand is attached.
entries.definitionCN: 被加上「千」这个前缀的基本单位。

entries.definition: A thousandth of a metre, the same unit with a smaller prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 一毫米，同一单位配更小的前缀。

entries.definition: An imperial distance of about one and six tenths kilometres.
entries.definitionCN: 英制距离，约一点六公里，与公里并用时常需换算。

entries.definition: The metric base unit of length.
entries.definitionCN: 公制的基本长度单位。

entries.definition: A short imperial length of about ninety centimetres.
entries.definitionCN: 英制短长度，约九十厘米。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to roads, speed limits, and the two languages that built it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把词绑在公路、限速和造出它的两种语言上。

normal.en: Kilo- means a thousand and metre means measure.
normal.cn: kilo- 意为千，metre 意为量度。

normal.en: The British write metre, the Americans write meter.
normal.cn: 英式写 metre，美式写 meter。

normal.en: Speed limits pair it with hour: kilometres per hour.
normal.cn: 限速牌把它和小时配对：每小时公里。

normal.en: Square it and it measures land.
normal.cn: 平方之后就用来量土地。

normal.en: Km on a road sign always stands for this word.
normal.cn: 路牌上的 km 永远代表这个词。

abstract.en: A kilometre is a thousand footsteps of the same length put end to end.
abstract.cn: 一公里就是把一千个等长的脚步首尾接起来。

abstract.en: Road signs turn the word into a promise about how much walking is left.
abstract.cn: 路牌把这个词变成一句承诺：还剩多少路要走。

abstract.en: One unit shared by every country means nobody has to convert at the border.
abstract.cn: 各国共用一种单位，意味着过境不必换算。

examples.en: The village is two kilometres from the sea.
examples.cn: 这个村子离海两公里。

examples.en: She runs ten kilometres every Sunday morning.
examples.cn: 她每个周日早上跑十公里。

examples.en: Prices are listed per kilometre of transport.
examples.cn: 运费按每公里列价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「kilometre」前半像「开了米」—— 开了一千米就是一公里

root: 由希腊语 khilioi（千）与 metron（量度）经法语复合而成，metre 为十八世纪末法国制定的长度单位，kilometre 即其后按同一模式造出的「千米」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses: the unit itself, distance on signs and maps, speed, area, and a loose spoken stretch of road.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项：单位本身、路牌与地图上的距离、速度、面积，以及口语里一段路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thousand strides laid end to end along a measured line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一千步等长的脚步沿一条量好的线首尾相接。

branches.en: THE SIGN LINE: the unit fixed on plates and maps.
branches.cn: 路牌这条线：单位被固定在牌子和地图上。

branches.en: THE SPEED LINE: distance per hour.
branches.cn: 速度这条线：每小时走多远。

branches.en: THE LAND LINE: the same unit squared for surfaces.
branches.cn: 土地这条线：同一单位平方之后量面积。

branches.en: THE RACE LINE: the last stretch that decides a run.
branches.cn: 赛程这条线：决定胜负的最后一段。

branches.en: THE TRAVEL LINE: every journey is counted in these units.
branches.cn: 旅程这条线：每一段路都用它来计数。

intro.en: The word is a compound whose pieces are all still working: a prefix, a base, a plural ending, and a two-letter symbol.
intro.cn: 这是个复合词，各部分至今都在使用：一个前缀、一个词基、一个复数词尾和两个字母的符号。

latinIntro.en: The parts came through Greek and French, so the entries below are Greek and French forms rather than native Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 构词成分经由希腊语和法语而来，下面的条目是希腊语与法语形式，而非本土拉丁语。

items.example: It is one kilometre to the bridge.
Ten kilometres is a long walk.
The room is four metres wide.

items.exampleCN: 图表里全是以公里计的距离。

definition_en: useful and easy for you, causing no trouble
core_image: 楼下的便利店，出门三步就能买到东西
scene: 新学期教室搬到了操场旁边，下课去图书馆更近了。 The new building is very convenient for students.
sceneCN: 这里 convenient 是「便利的」（第 1 个义项：省事、不添麻烦）；句意是新楼对学生来说很方便。

derivatives.zh: 由 convenient 加名词后缀构成，义为「便利；方便」
由 convenient 加 -ly 构成，义为「方便地」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不方便的」

senses.title: Easy to use or reach
senses.definition: useful because it saves you time or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 因省时省事而有用的
senses.example: The bus stop near our school is very convenient.
senses.exampleCN: 学校附近的公交站很方便。
senses.why: Latin venire means to come, and something convenient comes easily to meet your needs.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 venire 意为来到，便利之物轻松「来到」满足你的需要。

senses.title: Suitable; happening at the right time
senses.definition: fitting well with your plans or schedule
senses.definitionCN: 与你的计划或安排很契合
senses.example: Friday afternoon is a convenient time for our group meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 周五下午开小组会时间很合适。
senses.why: When things come together at the right moment, no one is troubled, so convenient also means suitable.
senses.whyCN: 事物恰好在合适的时刻齐聚，谁都不添麻烦，所以 convenient 也表示合适。

senses.title: Close by; handy in position
senses.definition: located near enough to be easy to use
senses.definitionCN: 位置足够近、用起来省事
senses.example: Our new flat is convenient to both the school and the park.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的新家离学校和公园都近。
senses.why: A place that comes close to you saves the journey, extending coming to location.
senses.whyCN: 离你近的地方省去了路途，把「来到」延伸到位置上。

intro.en: Convenient comes from Latin words about coming together.
intro.cn: convenient 来自拉丁语中「聚到一起」的表达。

items.en: The Latin verb convenire meant to come together or agree, from com- (together) + venire (to come).
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 convenire 意为聚在一起、一致，由 com-（共同）+ venire（来）构成。

items.en: The participle conveniens described things that fit well together.
items.cn: 分词 conveniens 形容彼此契合的事物。

items.en: French carried convenant and related forms meaning to agree.
items.cn: 法语用 convenant 及相关形式表示约定、同意。

items.en: English adopted convenient in the fourteenth century, first meaning agreeing or fitting.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 convenient，最初意为相合、契合。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the main meaning had moved to easy and useful.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，词义主流转向省事、有用。

note.en: These words share the ven root of coming, or mean easy to use.
note.cn: 这些词共享 ven（来）词根，或表示易用。

entries.definitionCN: 便利；方便

entries.definition: to gather people for a meeting

entries.definition: to come between and change a situation
entries.definitionCN: 干预；介入

entries.definitionCN: 发明（拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.cn: 把 convenient 和表示「来」的 ven 词根连起来记。

normal.en: convenient = com- (together) + venire (to come).
normal.cn: convenient 由 com-（共同）+ venire（来）构成。

normal.en: convene and intervention keep the ven root.
normal.cn: convene 和 intervention 都保留 ven 词根。

normal.en: convenience is the noun; a convenience store is handy.
normal.cn: convenience 是名词；便利店就是 handy 的店。

normal.en: in- makes inconvenient, the opposite.
normal.cn: 加 in- 构成 inconvenient，反义词。

normal.en: convenient sounds like can-ve-nyent; you can go there any moment.
normal.cn: convenient 发音像 can-ve-nyent，你随时都能去。

abstract.en: Picture a shop right next to the school gate.
abstract.cn: 想象紧挨校门的小店。

abstract.en: Picture your timetable and a meeting slot clicking together like puzzle pieces.
abstract.cn: 想象课程表和会议时段像拼图一样契合。

abstract.en: Picture stepping out of the lift right at your front door.
abstract.cn: 想象电梯门一开正好是家门口。

examples.en: It is convenient to take the subway to the museum.
examples.cn: 坐地铁去博物馆很方便。

examples.en: Please choose a convenient time for our video call.
examples.cn: 请选一个方便的时间视频通话。

examples.en: The convenience store near my home opens all night.
examples.cn: 我家附近的便利店通宵营业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯为你而特」——这家店肯为你特设窗口，办事真方便。

sensesIntro.en: From coming together to easy, suitable and nearby.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「聚到一起」引申为省事、合适与近便。

core.cn: 核心意象：事物轻松聚拢

intro.cn: 表示「来」的 ven 词根出现在许多英语词里。

definition_zh: 公平的；公正的；按规则行事的；浅色的；晴朗的；尚可的；相当多的；（旧）美丽的；（名词）集市、交易会
definition_en: treating people equally and following the rules, and, by older widening, light in colour, clear in weather, moderate in degree, handsome in appearance, or a gathering where goods are traded
core_image: 一架天平两端放着同样的砝码，指针停在正中，旁边摊开的规则手册对双方写着一模一样的条款
scene: 裁判在中线把球权判给先触球的一方，双方队员都照同一份规则手册行事。 The referee awarded the ball to the side that touched it first, and both teams played a fair game.
sceneCN: 这里指「按共同规则行事、不偏袒任何一方」，对应第 2 个义项：在竞赛或交易中依照事先约定的规则而不取巧；句意为裁判把球权判给先触球的一方，两队都按规则比赛。画面要点：中线、裁判手势、两队球衣、摊开的规则手册。

pos.zh: 公平的；公正的；按规则的；浅色的；晴朗的；尚可的；相当多的；（旧）美丽的
集市；交易会；博览会（另出一源，与形容词不同源）
公平地；按规则地（常用于表示按规则做事的固定说法）

collocations.zh: 公平的交易；公正的待遇

derivatives.zh: 公平；公正（基础词加古英语表性质的名词后缀，由形容词转为抽象状态）
公平地；相当地（基础词加副词后缀，语义由「公正」扩展到「程度适中」）
不公平的（否定前缀加基础词，指偏离规则或偏袒一方）
公正的；不偏不倚的（基础词与「心智」一词加过去分词后缀构成的复合形容词，指判断不受私利影响）
集市或博览会的场地（基础词与「地面」一词构成的复合名词，语义由交易会转向其举办场所）

senses.title: Even-handed in judgment
senses.titleCN: 判断时不偏袒任何一方
senses.definition: treating people equally and not letting personal preference decide an outcome
senses.definitionCN: 平等待人，不让个人好恶决定结果
senses.example: A fair judge hears both sides before ruling.
senses.exampleCN: 公正的法官在裁决前会听取双方陈述。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the word was 'beautiful, clean'; an unblemished decision was felt as something clean and pleasing, so the idea of even-handedness grew out of that older picture rather than from a word for law.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的意思是「美好的、洁净的」；不受污染的裁决被感受为洁净而令人愉悦之物，因此「公正」义是从那幅旧图景长出来的，而不是来自某个表示法律的词。

senses.title: According to the agreed rules
senses.titleCN: 依照事先约定的规则行事
senses.definition: played or done in the way the rules require, without trickery or advantage taken
senses.definitionCN: 按照规则要求去做，不取巧、不占便宜
senses.example: The referee awarded the ball to the side that touched it first, and both teams played a fair game.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判把球权判给先触球的一方，两队都按规则比赛。
senses.why: Once equal treatment is expected between opponents, the word names the conduct that keeps the contest equal, which is why sport fixed the phrase fair play.
senses.whyCN: 当对手之间被期待受到同等对待，这个词就用来指维持竞赛对等的行为，体育因此固定下「公平竞赛」这一说法。

senses.title: Light in colour
senses.definition: pale or light in colour, especially of hair, skin or cloth
senses.definitionCN: 颜色浅淡，尤指头发、皮肤或织物
senses.example: The child had fair hair and a sunburned nose.
senses.exampleCN: 那孩子头发浅淡，鼻子晒得发红。
senses.why: A clean, bright appearance was the core of the old sense, and lightness of colour is exactly what that brightness looks like on a surface.
senses.whyCN: 洁净明亮的外观是旧义的核心，而颜色的浅淡正是这种明亮落在表面上的样子。

senses.title: Clear and cloudless weather
senses.definition: bright and dry, with no rain and little cloud
senses.definitionCN: 明亮干燥、无雨少云
senses.example: The forecast promised fair weather for the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 预报说渡海期间天气晴好。
senses.why: A sky without cloud shares the same visual core of brightness and cleanliness, so the weather sense needs no separate origin.
senses.whyCN: 无云的天空共享同一个明亮洁净的视觉核心，因此天气义无需另找来源。

senses.title: Moderately good, no more
senses.definition: acceptable but not excellent; average in quality
senses.definitionCN: 可以接受但不算出色；质量中等
senses.example: The hotel was fair, neither luxurious nor shabby.
senses.exampleCN: 那家旅馆还算可以，既不豪华也不破旧。
senses.why: In grading, 'pleasing enough' slid downward from praise to mere adequacy, and the old phrase fair to middling fixed the middling reading.
senses.whyCN: 在评级中，「足够令人满意」从称赞滑向仅仅及格，旧说法「尚可、中不溜」把这种中等义固定了下来。

senses.title: Considerable in size or amount
senses.definition: large enough to be worth noticing, though not stated exactly
senses.definitionCN: 大到值得注意，但没有确切说出数量
senses.example: A fair number of students stayed after class to ask questions.
senses.exampleCN: 相当多的学生下课后留下来提问。
senses.why: The 'handsome, ample' reading came from the sense of something fine and substantial, not from justice, which is why a fair amount can be large without being equal.
senses.whyCN: 「可观、充足」这一读法来自「美好而结实」的意思，与公正无关；所以「相当多的量」可以很大，却与平等无关。

senses.title: Beautiful, in older use
senses.definition: lovely to look at, used of women in older literature and ballads
senses.definitionCN: 容貌秀美，旧文学与民谣中用于形容女子
senses.example: The fair maiden in the old ballad waited by the well.
senses.exampleCN: 古老民谣里那位美丽的少女在井边等候。
senses.why: This is the earliest recorded sense and the source of all the others; it survives in fixed literary phrases rather than in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 这是有记录的最早义项，也是其余义项的源头；它只残留在固定的文学说法里，不再用于日常口语。

senses.title: A gathering where goods are traded
senses.titleCN: 集市、交易会（名词，另出一源）
senses.definition: a large outdoor or indoor event where stalls and companies show and sell goods
senses.definitionCN: 在户外或室内举办、由摊位与公司展示并销售商品的大型活动
senses.example: Farmers brought wool and cheese to the annual fair.
senses.exampleCN: 农民把羊毛和奶酪带到一年一度的集市上。
senses.why: The noun is a different word: Latin feria 'festival day' came through Old French and fell together with the adjective in spelling, so the market sense has no link to justice.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是另一个词：拉丁语中意为「节日」的词经古法语传入，拼写上才与形容词合流，因此集市义与公正义并无牵连。

intro.en: Fair as an adjective comes from Old English fæger 'beautiful, pleasant, clean', a Germanic word with recorded relatives in Gothic. The noun for a market is a separate borrowing from Latin feria 'festival day'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 作形容词的 fair 来自古英语 fæger「美好的、愉悦的、洁净的」，属日耳曼语词，哥特语中有可考的同族形式。作「集市」解的名词另出拉丁 feria「节日」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Fæger meant 'beautiful, pleasant, clean' and was applied to people, weather, land and objects alike. All the later senses grow from this single descriptive word.
items.cn: fæger 意为「美好的、愉悦的、洁净的」，可用于人、天气、土地与器物。后来各义项都从这一个描写性词生长出来。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form *fagraz is posited as the common ancestor; Gothic fagrs 'fitting, suitable' is its closest recorded relative. The starred form is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 学界拟构的日耳曼语形式 *fagraz 被推为共同祖先；哥特语 fagrs「合适的、相称的」是它最近的可考同族词。带星号的形式属重构形式，并非有文献实证的词。

items.en: Source uncertain: no accepted Indo-European ancestor is established for the Germanic adjective. A connection with a root meaning 'to make beautiful' has been suggested, but it remains a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个日耳曼形容词尚无公认的印欧语祖先。有人提出它与一个意为「使美」的词根相关，但那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: By the Middle English period the word described decisions and dealings that were clean of bias, and this equitable sense became the dominant everyday one.
items.cn: 到中古英语时期，这个词已用来描述不带偏私的裁决与交易，这一公正义随后成为日常使用中的主导义。

items.en: Light hair and cloudless skies were both called fair because both shared the old core of clean brightness; neither sense required a new source.
items.cn: 浅色的头发与无云的天空都被称作 fair，因为两者都共享「洁净明亮」这一旧核心；这两个义项都不需要新的来源。

items.en: The market noun descends from Latin feria 'festival day', through Old French feire. It is homonymous with the adjective only in modern spelling; the two words are unrelated at the root.
items.cn: 「集市」这一名词出自拉丁 feria「节日」，经古法语 feire 传入。它只在现代拼写上与形容词同形；两个词在词根上并无关联。

note.en: The first group holds look-alikes and homophones that are constantly mistaken for this word; the second group holds near alternatives for the idea of even-handedness.
note.cn: 第一组是极易与这个词混淆的形近词与同音词；第二组是「不偏不倚」这一意思的近义替代。

entries.definition: The money paid for a journey, or food provided; it comes from an Old English word for a journey, not from the adjective for beauty or justice.
entries.definitionCN: 旅费或供应的饮食；出自古英语中表示「行程」的词，与表示美好或公正的形容词无关。

entries.definition: A small magical being; the word comes from Old French faerie 'enchantment', so the resemblance to fair is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 一种小巧的魔法生灵；该词出自古法语中表示「魔法、魅惑」的词，因此与「美好」一词的相似只是巧合。

entries.definition: The adverb of fair, but it splits into 'in a just manner' and 'to a moderate degree', the second being far more common in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 这是该形容词的副词形式，但分成「以公正的方式」与「达到中等程度」两读，后者在口语中常见得多。

entries.definition: A deliberately archaic spelling of the market noun, used by organisers to suggest a traditional festival; it adds no new meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 「集市」这一名词故意仿古的拼法，主办方用它暗示传统节庆；并不增添新义。

entries.definition: Conforming to what is morally right or lawful; it judges the outcome, while fair stresses the equal treatment that produced it.
entries.definitionCN: 符合道德上正确或法律上正当的要求；它评判结果，而本词更强调产生结果时的平等待遇。

entries.definition: Fair in a formal or legal setting, often correcting a strict rule to reach a balanced result; it is the technical counterpart of the plainer word.
entries.definitionCN: 在正式或法律语境中表示公平，常用来修正过严的规则以取得平衡结果；它是较朴素那个词的专业对应词。

entries.definition: Not favouring one party over another; it describes the absence of bias, whereas fair can also praise a positive even-handedness.
entries.definitionCN: 不偏袒任何一方；它描述的是没有偏见，而本词还可称赞一种积极的持平态度。

entries.definition: Light in colour, often suggesting less brightness than normal; it covers one sense of fair but never carries judgment or weather.
entries.definitionCN: 颜色浅，常暗示比正常情况少了些血色或亮度；它只覆盖其中一个义项，从不带判断或天气之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the recorded Old English sense, real derived words and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：有文献可考的古英语义项、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The oldest sense is 'beautiful, clean', so a fair decision is pictured as an unblemished surface.
normal.cn: 最古老的意思是「美好的、洁净的」，因此公正的裁决被想象成一块没有污点的表面。

normal.en: The family runs fair, fairly, fairness, unfair, fair-minded and fairground.
normal.cn: 同族词包括本词及其副词形式、表性质的名词、否定形式与复合形式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the senses: fair play, fair weather, fair hair, a fair amount, a trade fair.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把各义项分开：公平竞赛、晴朗天气、浅色头发、相当多的量、贸易博览会。

normal.en: Fare, the price of a journey, sounds identical but belongs to a different Old English word.
normal.cn: 表示旅费的另一个同音词读音完全相同，却属于另一个古英语词。

normal.en: The market noun came from Latin feria 'festival day', so a county fair and a fair judgment are unrelated at the root.
normal.cn: 表示集市的名词出自拉丁语中意为「节日」的词，因此乡村集市与公正裁决在词根上毫不相干。

abstract.en: Picture a balance whose two pans carry different weights but whose beam stays level because the rulebook sits on the fulcrum.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，两只托盘放着不同的重量，横梁却保持水平，因为规则手册就垫在支点上。

abstract.en: Picture a white sky over a pale field, the same brightness spread across weather, hair and cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象苍白田野上方的白色天空，同一种明亮铺在天气、头发与布料上。

abstract.en: Picture two separate rivers that happen to join at one estuary: one carries an old song, the other a holiday crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象两条本不相干的河流恰在同一河口汇合：一条载着古老的歌，一条载着过节的人群。

examples.en: The committee reached a fair settlement that both sides could accept.
examples.cn: 委员会达成了一个双方都能接受的公平和解。

examples.en: Fair weather held until the boats were halfway across the bay.
examples.cn: 晴好的天气一直持续到船只驶过海湾中段。

examples.en: She keeps a fair number of old maps in the bottom drawer.
examples.cn: 她在最下面的抽屉里存着相当多的旧地图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费厄」——费厄泼赖就是按规则公平竞赛，凡事照同一本规则来 → 公平的、按规则的

root: 古英语 fæger「美好的、洁净的」，与哥特语 fagrs「相称的」同族；更深来源不确定，有「使美」词根的假说，属重构形式。名词「集市」义另出拉丁 feria「节日」，经古法语 feire 借入，与形容词不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses fan out from one picture: a surface that is clean and bright. That brightness becomes light colour, then clear weather, then a beautiful person, then a decision with no stain on it. From the unstained decision come rule-bound play, mere adequacy and a sizeable amount, while the market sense enters English by a separate Latin road.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一幅图景展开：一块洁净明亮的表面。这种明亮先成为浅色，再成为晴朗，再成为美丽的容貌，再成为没有污点的裁决。从无污点的裁决又分出依规则行事、仅够及格与数量可观；而集市义则沿着另一条拉丁语道路进入英语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clean, bright surface on which no stain or tilt can be seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块洁净明亮的表面，看不出任何污点或倾斜。

branches.en: UNSTAINED JUDGMENT: the ethical reading, where no personal preference leaves a mark on the outcome.
branches.cn: 无污点的判断：伦理层面的读法，个人好恶不在结果上留下痕迹。

branches.en: RULES AND ADEQUACY: equal conduct between opponents, and the milder reading of 'good enough' that grading produced.
branches.cn: 规则与及格：对手之间的对等行为，以及评级产生的「还算可以」这一较弱读法。

branches.en: BRIGHTNESS ON A SURFACE: light hair and cloudless sky are the old brightness seen outdoors and on a body.
branches.cn: 表面上的明亮：浅色头发与无云天空，是那种旧有的明亮落在户外与人身上。

branches.en: AMPLE AND LOVELY: a handsome size, and the oldest literary sense of beauty that started the whole family.
branches.cn: 充足与秀美：可观的规模，以及开启整个词族的最早文学义「美」。

branches.en: SEPARATE MARKET WORD: a festival day borrowed from Latin, joined only by spelling.
branches.cn: 另源的集市词：从拉丁语借来的节日，只靠拼写与前者合流。

intro.en: Fair is a native English adjective whose endings are Germanic, while the market noun arrived separately from Latin, so the family carries two unrelated histories.
intro.cn: 该词是英语本族的形容词，其词尾属日耳曼语；而表示集市的名词另从拉丁语传入，因此这个词族携带两段互不相干的历史。

latinIntro.en: The adjective has no Latin source. The Latin forms below belong only to the market noun, and the Latin word for a festival day is not related to the adjective for beauty or justice.
latinIntro.cn: 这个形容词没有拉丁语来源。下列拉丁形式只属于表示集市的名词；拉丁语中表示节日的词，与表示美或公正的形容词并无关联。

items.example: Both teams played a fair game.
The review questioned the fairness of the test.
items.exampleCN: 评审质疑这项测试的公平性。

items.example: It was unfair to single out one applicant.
items.exampleCN: 单独挑出一名申请者是不公平的。

items.meaningCN: 愿意不带偏见地判断的
items.example: A fair-minded reader will check the sources.
items.exampleCN: 公正的读者会去核对来源。

items.meaning: the site of a market or show
items.example: Trucks queued at the gate of the fairground.
items.exampleCN: 卡车在集市场地门口排队。

items.meaning: loyal only while things go well
items.example: A fair-weather ally left when the storm came.
items.exampleCN: 一个只能同甘的盟友在风暴来时就离开了。

items.example: The coach praised the visiting side for its fair play.
items.exampleCN: 教练称赞客队遵守规则。

items.structure: fayre (revived spelling of the market noun)
items.meaningCN: 仿古拼写的集市或节庆
items.example: The village held a summer fayre on the green.
items.exampleCN: 村子在草地上举办了夏季集市。

derivatives.zh: 公平；公正（基础词加表性质的名词后缀，由形容词转为抽象状态）
公正地；相当地（基础词加副词后缀，语义扩展到程度适中）
不公平的（否定前缀加基础词，指偏袒或违背规则）
公正的（基础词与「心智」复合再加分词后缀，指判断不受私利左右）

definition_en: the direction where the sun rises, or the part of a country or world that lies that way
core_image: 清晨太阳从地平线升起的那一边
scene: 海边的清晨，渔民背对着朝阳收网归来。 The fishing boats sailed east along the calm coast.
sceneCN: 这里 east 是「向东」（第 2 个义项：朝东方的方向移动）；句意：渔船沿着平静的海岸向东航行。

derivatives.zh: east 加 ern 构成，义为「东方的；东部的」
east 加 ward 构成，义为「向东」

senses.title: The direction of sunrise
senses.definition: the point of the horizon where the sun rises
senses.definitionCN: 地平线上太阳升起的方位
senses.example: The temple gate faces east to greet the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 寺庙大门朝东，迎接日出。
senses.why: The oldest anchor is the daily sunrise itself.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的锚点就是每日的日出。

senses.title: Movement or position toward east
senses.definition: moving or lying in the east direction
senses.definitionCN: 朝东的方向移动或位于东方
senses.example: The fishing boats sailed east along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 渔船沿着海岸向东航行。
senses.why: The direction becomes a path to travel.
senses.whyCN: 方位变成一条可走的路径。

senses.title: The eastern part of a region
senses.definition: the part of a country, continent, or world that lies toward the east
senses.definitionCN: 国家、大陆或世界的东部区域
senses.example: Rain is coming from the east of the province.
senses.exampleCN: 雨正从该省东部过来。
senses.why: The small direction grows into a wide human region.
senses.whyCN: 小小的方位长成广阔的人文地域。

intro.en: East is a Germanic sky word, tied to the brightness of dawn.
intro.cn: east 是一个日耳曼的天空词，与黎明的光亮相连。

items.en: Proto-Germanic *austam meant the direction of dawn, related to a word for shine.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语 *austam 意为黎明的方向，与表示「闪耀」的词相关。

items.en: Old English ēast named both sunrise and the eastern lands.
items.cn: 古英语 ēast 既指日出之方，也指东方之地。

items.en: Old Norse austr kept the same dawn direction in Viking sailing.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 austr 在维京航海中保留同一黎明方位。

items.en: Middle English used east for maps, trade winds and eastern peoples.
items.cn: 中古英语把 east 用于地图、信风与东方民族。

items.en: Modern English built eastern, eastward and East Asia.
items.cn: 现代英语构出 eastern、eastward 与 East Asia 等。

note.en: These words stand near east in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 east 相邻。

entries.definition: of the east
entries.definitionCN: 东方的

entries.definition: not difficult, different root
entries.definitionCN: 容易的（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: toward the east
entries.definitionCN: 向东

entries.definition: the direction of sunset
entries.definitionCN: 西；西方

entries.definition: the east, formal or literary
entries.definitionCN: 东方（正式或文学用语）

entries.definition: the time the sun rises
entries.definitionCN: 日出

normalIntro.en: Use the sunrise picture and the east family.
normalIntro.cn: 用「日出」的画面和 east 词族来记。

normal.en: east is where the sun rises every morning.
normal.cn: east 是每天太阳升起的方向。

normal.en: eastern adds ern for the adjective.
normal.cn: eastern 加 ern 构成形容词。

normal.en: the east wind blows from the east.
normal.cn: 东风从东方吹来。

normal.en: sail east means head toward sunrise.
normal.cn: sail east 就是朝日出的方向航行。

normal.en: remember east and west never meet on a straight line.
normal.cn: 记住 east 与 west 在直线上永不相交。

abstract.en: Stand on a shore and watch light spill from one horizon point.
abstract.cn: 站在岸边，看光从地平线的一点洒出。

abstract.en: Feel your face warmed first on the east side.
abstract.cn: 感受脸的东侧最先被阳光晒暖。

abstract.en: Follow a compass needle pointing to dawn.
abstract.cn: 跟随指向黎明的罗盘指针。

examples.en: The kitchen window faces east, so mornings are bright.
examples.cn: 厨房窗户朝东，所以早晨很亮堂。

examples.en: Walk east for ten minutes and you will see the market.
examples.cn: 向东走十分钟就能看到市场。

examples.en: Rain clouds gathered over the eastern hills.
examples.cn: 雨云在东部群山上空聚集。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「依斯特」——太阳「依」着「斯特」这条线从东方升起

root: 来自原始日耳曼语 *austam（黎明的方向），与表示「闪耀」的词根相关，古英语 ēast；本义即日出之处，后指东方地域。

sensesIntro.en: East starts at the sunrise point, then becomes a path and finally a wide region.
sensesIntro.cn: east 从日出之点出发，变成行进方向，最后指辽阔的东方地域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the horizon point where dawn breaks
core.cn: 核心意象：黎明破晓的地平线之点

branches.en: The point where light first appears
The path toward that point
The wide land on that side
Whatever follows the morning light
The compass role in naming places
branches.cn: 罗盘在命名地域中的角色

intro.en: East builds a small compass family of eastern and eastward.
intro.cn: east 构成 eastern、eastward 等小小的罗盘词族。

latinIntro.en: East is Germanic in origin, so it has no Latin relatives; orient is the Latin word for the rising sun.
latinIntro.cn: east 源自日耳曼语，因此没有拉丁同族词；拉丁语表示日出之方的词是 orient。

items.example: the sun rises in the east

items.meaning: having the quality of a direction
the act of facing a direction

latinEntries.meaning: the rising sun, the east; source of orient
latinEntries.meaningCN: 日出的太阳、东方；orient 的来源

definition_zh: 梯子；阶梯；晋升阶梯；（长袜的）抽丝
definition_en: a frame with rungs used for climbing; also a graded series of levels, a run in a stocking, or to climb by means of a ladder
core_image: 靠在墙边的木梯，一级一级通向高处
scene: 仓库的屋顶坏了一块，师傅把梯子靠在墙边，仰头看了看上面的缺口。 He climbed the ladder to fix the roof tiles before the rain came.
sceneCN: 这里是「梯子」（第 1 个义项：供人攀爬的用具）；句意是他在下雨前爬上梯子修屋顶的瓦片。图中可辨识物件：木梯、砖墙、屋顶缺口。

pos.zh: 用梯子攀爬；使织物抽丝

derivatives.zh: 由 ladder 加 -ed 构成，义为「有梯级的；抽丝的」
由 ladder 加 -ing 构成，义为「织物抽丝；阶梯式安排」
由 ladder 与 like 复合而成，义为「梯状的」

senses.title: A frame used for climbing
senses.definition: a set of steps or rungs joined by two side pieces, used to reach high places
senses.definitionCN: 由两侧支柱连接若干横档组成、用来够到高处的攀爬用具
senses.example: The painter left the ladder against the wall overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 油漆工把梯子靠在墙边过了一夜。
senses.why: Old English hlæder named a leaning frame, and that concrete object is still the first sense anyone pictures.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hlæder 指可以斜靠的架子，所以这个具体物件仍是人们最先想到的义项。

senses.title: A graded series of levels
senses.definition: a sequence of ranks or stages that someone moves through, especially in a career
senses.definitionCN: 某人依次经历的一串等级或阶段，尤指职业上的晋升
senses.example: She worked her way up the corporate ladder one promotion at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 她沿着企业晋升阶梯，一步一步往上走。
senses.why: A real ladder is climbed rung by rung, so the same picture is borrowed for any ranked order that is advanced one stage at a time.
senses.whyCN: 真正的梯子要一级一级往上爬，于是同一幅画面被借来形容任何逐级上升的等级序列。

senses.title: A run in stockings or tights
senses.definition: a long tear in a stocking or pair of tights that spreads in a line
senses.definitionCN: 长袜或连裤袜上沿一条线延伸的裂口
senses.example: A ladder in her tights forced her to change before the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 长袜上的一处抽丝让她不得不在开会前换掉。
senses.why: The thin line of a run looks like a row of rungs running down the fabric, which is why British English calls it a ladder.
senses.whyCN: 抽丝形成的那道细线像一排横档顺着织物往下走，英式英语因此把它叫作 ladder。

senses.title: To climb with or as if with a ladder
senses.titleCN: 用梯子攀爬；借助梯状物攀升
senses.definition: to climb or reach something using a ladder, or to move up as if using one
senses.definitionCN: 借助梯子爬向或够到某处，也指像踩梯子一样向上移动
senses.example: The rescue team laddered the cliff and reached the stranded hikers.
senses.exampleCN: 救援队借助梯状绳索攀上崖壁，到达被困的徒步者身边。
senses.why: The noun came first; turning it into a verb simply adds the action of using the object, in the same way that brush became to brush.
senses.whyCN: 名词先出现，把它用作动词只是补上「使用这个物件」的动作，就像 brush 变成 to brush 一样。

intro.en: Ladder is an old Germanic word with no Latin ancestor; English has carried it from a leaning frame to ranked levels and torn stockings.
intro.cn: ladder 是古老的日耳曼语词，没有拉丁语祖先；英语把它从斜靠的架子一路用到等级阶梯和长袜抽丝。

items.en: A distant root is sometimes suggested, but the reconstruction is uncertain and should not be treated as settled.
items.cn: 有时会提出一个更古老的远祖词根，但该重构并不确定，不宜当作定论。

items.en: The Germanic form is reconstructed as hlaidrijō, naming something that leans or is propped up.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式常重构为 hlaidrijō，指可以倚靠或支撑起来的东西。

items.en: Old English hlæder already meant a ladder, and the word appears in texts about building and farming.
items.cn: 古英语 hlæder 已指梯子，这个词见于建筑与农事文本。

items.en: Middle English smoothed the consonant cluster and wrote ladder, the spelling English still uses.
items.cn: 中古英语简化了辅音组合，写作 ladder，也就是今天沿用的拼写。

items.en: Modern English extended the noun to ranks and to a run in fabric, and turned it into a verb of climbing.
items.cn: 现代英语把名词扩展到等级和织物抽丝，并派生出表示攀爬的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and suffixes built on ladder; the near-meaning group collects things climbed or stepped on.
note.cn: 形近组收由 ladder 构成的复合词与加缀词；近义组收供人攀爬、踩踏的同类事物。

entries.definition: A folding ladder with steps instead of plain rungs.
entries.definitionCN: 一种带踏步而非普通横档的折叠梯；梯凳。

entries.definition: Marked with a run, or fitted with rungs.
entries.definitionCN: 有抽丝的；装有横档的。

entries.definition: The forming of a run in tights, or the arranging of levels.
entries.definitionCN: 长袜抽丝；阶梯式的层级安排。

entries.definition: The second of two things mentioned; only the spelling is close, since the history of the word is different.
entries.definitionCN: 两者中的后者；只是拼写相近，词源并不相同。

entries.definition: A set of steps built into a building for going up and down.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物内固定安装、供上下行走的一段楼梯。

entries.definition: The whole structure of stairs, including its frame and handrail.
entries.definitionCN: 楼梯的整体结构，包括框架与扶手。

entries.definition: One of the crossbars that form the steps of a ladder.
entries.definitionCN: 梯子上构成踏步的一根横档。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic simplex noun, and its compounds and suffixes move it from a climbing tool to rank and to torn fabric.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语的单纯名词，复合词与后缀把它从攀爬工具延伸到等级和抽丝的织物。

normal.en: Old English hlæder became ladder by smoothing the consonant cluster, so the modern form is a shortened, easier mouthful.
normal.cn: 古英语 hlæder 经过辅音简化变成 ladder，所以现代拼写是更省力的一串音。

normal.en: Ladder belongs to the Germanic layer of English, not to the Latin layer, so it has no Latin relative to learn with it.
normal.cn: ladder 属于英语的日耳曼语层，而不是拉丁语层，所以不必为它硬找拉丁同族词。

normal.en: Stepladder is simply step plus ladder: a ladder whose steps are broad boards rather than thin rungs.
normal.cn: stepladder 就是 step 加 ladder：踏板是宽板而不是细横档的梯子。

normal.en: Rung is the name of a single crossbar, which is why climbing a ladder means moving from rung to rung.
normal.cn: rung 是单根横档的名字，所以爬梯子就是一级横档一级横档地移动。

normal.en: The corporate ladder keeps the climbing picture and turns each promotion into one more rung.
normal.cn: corporate ladder 保留了攀爬的画面，把每一次晋升都变成又一级横档。

abstract.en: A tool that exists only to raise a person explains why the word so easily becomes a picture of ambition.
abstract.cn: 一种只为把人送高的工具，解释了为什么这个词很容易变成野心的图画。

abstract.en: The same thin line that marks a climb also marks a tear, so ascent and damage share one shape.
abstract.cn: 标记攀爬的那道细线也能标记裂口，于是上升与破损共用了同一种形状。

abstract.en: Ladder reminds us that height is reached in small, repeated moves rather than in one leap.
abstract.cn: ladder 提醒人：高度是靠一次次小移动到达的，而不是一步跃上去的。

examples.en: The painter left the ladder against the wall overnight.
examples.cn: 油漆工把梯子靠在墙边过了一夜。

examples.en: She worked her way up the corporate ladder one promotion at a time.
examples.cn: 她沿着企业晋升阶梯，一步一步往上走。

examples.en: A ladder in her tights forced her to change before the meeting.
examples.cn: 长袜上的一处抽丝让她不得不在开会前换掉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累的」——爬梯子爬到腿都累了；记住 ladder 是梯子。

root: 古英语 hlæder，属日耳曼语固有词；一般认为与表示「倾斜、倚靠」的词有远亲关系，与拉丁语没有直接同源关系。

sensesIntro.en: The concrete climbing frame is the core; from it come the ranked ladder of promotion, the ladder-like run in fabric, and the verb of climbing.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是具体的攀爬架子；由此分出表示晋升的等级阶梯、织物上梯状的抽丝，以及表示攀爬的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden ladder leaning against a wall, its rungs leading upward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把木梯靠在墙边，横档一级级通向高处。

branches.en: a wooden frame leaning against a wall
hands moving from rung to rung in the dark
branches.cn: 黑暗中双手一级一级向上移动

branches.en: a chart where each box is a promotion
branches.cn: 每一格代表一次晋升的图表

branches.en: a climb that never seems to end
branches.cn: 一场仿佛没有尽头的攀升

branches.en: a thin line running down a stocking
branches.cn: 长袜上向下延伸的一道细线

intro.en: A Germanic noun is extended by one compound with step and by two suffixes that produce an adjective and a noun.
intro.cn: 这个日耳曼语名词由 step 构成的复合词，以及两个分别造出形容词和名词的后缀来扩展。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

one rung or a movement of the foot
marked with a run or with rungs

definition_zh: 挑战；难题；质疑；向……挑战；质疑
definition_en: a demanding task that tests ability; an invitation to compete; to question the truth of something
core_image: 有人把战书掷到你面前，要你应战或接受考验
scene: 运动会上，隔壁班向我们班下了长跑比赛的战书。 The relay race was a real challenge for our team.
sceneCN: 这里 challenge 是「挑战；难题」（第 1 个义项：考验能力的困难任务）；句意为接力赛对我们队是真正的挑战。

derivatives.zh: 由 challenge 加 -ing 构成，义为「有挑战性的；困难的」
由 challenge 加 -er 构成，义为「挑战者」

senses.title: A demanding task that tests ability
senses.definition: a difficult task or problem that tests someone's ability or effort
senses.definitionCN: 考验能力或努力的困难任务或问题
senses.example: Learning a new language is a big challenge.
senses.exampleCN: 学习一门新语言是个大挑战。
senses.why: The old contest call became a name for any hard task, because a hard task also dares you to try.
senses.whyCN: 古老的叫阵声变成了困难任务的代名词，因为困难同样在向你的能力叫板。

senses.title: An invitation to compete or fight
senses.definition: an invitation to take part in a contest or fight to see who is better
senses.definitionCN: 邀请参加比赛或较量，看谁更强
senses.example: He threw down a challenge to a chess game after school.
senses.exampleCN: 他下战后书，约对方放学后下一盘棋。
senses.why: This is the word's oldest sense: formally calling someone out to prove who wins.
senses.whyCN: 这是词的最古老义项：正式叫人出来一决高下。

senses.title: To question the truth or rightness of something
senses.definition: to say that something may not be true or right, and ask for proof
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事未必真实或正确，要求拿出证据
senses.example: She challenged the answer and asked the teacher to check it again.
senses.exampleCN: 她质疑那个答案，请老师再核对一次。
senses.why: To challenge someone once meant to accuse them, so questioning a claim is like calling it to defend itself.
senses.whyCN: challenge 曾指指控某人，质疑一个说法就像叫它出来自证。

senses.title: To invite someone to compete
senses.definition: to formally ask someone to compete against you
senses.definitionCN: 正式邀请某人与自己比赛
senses.example: Our class challenged Class Two to a basketball match.
senses.exampleCN: 我们班向二班发起篮球比赛挑战。
senses.why: The contest call itself became a verb: to challenge is to give the call.
senses.whyCN: 叫阵的名词本身转为动词：challenge 就是发出叫阵。

intro.en: Challenge comes from a Latin word for calling someone out by name, passing through Old French into English.
intro.cn: challenge 源自拉丁语中指「点名叫出某人」的词，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Latin calumnia meant a false accusation or legal claim, later shaped into calumniari, to accuse falsely.
items.cn: 拉丁语 calumnia 指诬告或法律指控，后形成动词 calumniari（诬告）。

items.en: Old French chalonge meant a claim, complaint or accusation in law.
items.cn: 古法语 chalonge 指法律上的主张、控诉或申诉。

items.en: Middle English chalenge first meant to accuse or claim something as one's right.
items.cn: 中古英语 chalenge 先指指控或主张某种权利。

items.en: The sense shifted to calling someone out to a contest or duel.
items.cn: 词义转为叫人出来比赛或决斗。

items.en: Modern English uses challenge for contests, hard tasks and questioning claims.
items.cn: 现代英语的 challenge 涵盖比赛、难题和质疑之义。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects related contest and doubt words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收比赛与质疑类词。

entries.definition: To make or become different.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「改变」，拼写与 challenge 相近。

entries.definition: The person who challenges.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「挑战者」，由 challenge 派生。

entries.definition: A French sparkling wine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「香槟酒」，读音与 challenge 词首相近。

entries.definition: A competition between people or teams.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「竞赛」，与 challenge 的比赛义相近。

entries.definition: To feel unsure that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「怀疑」，与 challenge 的质疑义相近。

entries.definition: To ask about or express doubt about something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「质疑；询问」，与 challenge 相近。

normalIntro.en: Remember challenge by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 challenge。

normal.en: the root goes back to Latin calumnia, a legal accusation.
normal.cn: 词根可追溯到拉丁语 calumnia（法律指控）。

normal.en: challenger is the one who challenges.
normal.cn: challenger 就是发出挑战的人。

normal.en: challenging describes a task that tests you.
normal.cn: challenging 形容考验人的难事。

normal.en: throw down the challenge is a fixed picture of starting a contest.
normal.cn: throw down the challenge（掷下战书）是开赛的固定画面。

normal.en: rise to the challenge means to meet a hard task bravely.
normal.cn: rise to the challenge 意为勇敢迎接难题。

abstract.en: Picture a glove thrown to the ground before a duel.
abstract.cn: 想象决斗前掷落在地上的一只手套。

abstract.en: Hear a rival calling your name across the field.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见对手隔着场地喊出你的名字。

abstract.en: Feel the pull of a mountain daring you to climb.
abstract.cn: 感受一座大山向你发出的攀登邀请。

examples.en: The relay race was a real challenge for our team.
examples.cn: 接力赛对我们队是一次真正的挑战。

examples.en: Our class challenged Class Three to a football match.
examples.cn: 我们班向三班发起足球赛挑战。

examples.en: She challenged the result and asked for a recount.
examples.cn: 她对结果提出质疑，要求重新统计。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「差冷之」——差生冷不丁之一句「不服来战」，这就是挑战。

root: 拉丁语 calumnia（诬告）→ 古法语 chalonge（控诉、主张）→ 中古英语 chalenge → 现代英语 challenge；派生词有 challenger（挑战者）、challenging（有挑战性的）。

sensesIntro.en: Challenge moves from a legal call-out to a contest call, then to hard tasks and doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: challenge 由法律叫阵转为比赛叫阵，再延伸到难题与质疑。

core.cn: 核心意象：叫人出来一决是非高下

intro.cn: challenge 由拉丁语中叫人对质的法律词演变而来。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 calumni- 解释了这个词「指控」的过去。

items.example: This is a challenging maths problem.
items.exampleCN: 这是一道有挑战性的数学题。

items.example: The challenger lost the boxing match.
items.exampleCN: 挑战者输了这场拳击赛。

items.meaning: a prize that teams compete to win
items.example: Our school won the challenge cup.
items.exampleCN: 我们学校赢得了挑战杯。

items.example: He threw down a challenge to the best player.
items.exampleCN: 他向最强的选手下了战书。

items.meaning: to deal well with a hard task
items.example: She rose to the challenge of the exam.
items.exampleCN: 她迎着考试的挑战而上。

items.example: We are ready to meet the challenge.

items.meaning: a question that doubts an answer
items.example: He raised a challenge question in class.

items.exampleCN: 这些数据是可以质疑的。

definition_en: to move quickly; to do something too fast; a sudden attack; a busy period
core_image: 人群或水流一下子朝一个方向猛冲
scene: 她抓起包就冲出了门。 She grabbed her bag and rushed out of the door.
sceneCN: 这里 rush 是「冲」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她抓起包就冲出了门。

derivatives.zh: 仓促的；匆忙的
急速流动的
高峰时段

senses.title: Move quickly
senses.definition: to move with great speed
senses.definitionCN: 以极快的速度移动
senses.example: She rushed to the station.
senses.exampleCN: 她冲向车站。
senses.why: The core sense is sudden fast motion.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是突然的快速运动。

senses.title: Do too fast
senses.definition: to do something too quickly
senses.definitionCN: 过于仓促地做某事
senses.example: Don't rush the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 不要仓促作决定。
senses.why: Fast motion becomes hasty action.
senses.whyCN: 快速移动变成草率行事。

senses.title: Sudden attack
senses.definition: a sudden military attack
senses.definitionCN: 突然的军事攻击
senses.example: The soldiers rushed the gate at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们在黎明时冲向大门。
senses.why: Charging forward becomes an assault.
senses.whyCN: 向前冲变成进攻。

senses.title: Busy period
senses.definition: a busy period when many people move
senses.definitionCN: 许多人同时涌动的繁忙时段
senses.example: The morning rush fills every train.
senses.exampleCN: 早高峰让每列火车都挤满人。
senses.why: The movement becomes a crowded time.
senses.whyCN: 运动变成拥挤的时段。

intro.en: Rush comes from Old French ruser, to drive back or charge.
intro.cn: rush 源自古法语 ruser，意为击退、猛冲。

items.en: Ruser means to drive back or push.
items.cn: ruser 意为击退或推挤。

items.en: Russher means to charge forward.
items.cn: russher 意为向前猛冲。

items.en: Rushen covers people and water.
items.cn: rushen 兼指人与水流。

items.en: Rush extends to hasty action.
items.cn: rush 扩展到仓促行事。

items.en: Rush hour names the busiest travel time.
items.cn: rush hour 指最繁忙的通行时段。

note.en: Rush is fast movement; rust is a red coat on iron.
note.cn: rush 是快速冲撞，rust 则是铁上的锈。

entries.definitionCN: 冲锋

normalIntro.en: Rush is speed with little time to think.
normalIntro.cn: rush 是快得来不及思考的速度。

normal.en: People rush for the last train.
normal.cn: 人们冲向末班车。

normal.en: Do not rush your homework.
normal.cn: 不要急着赶作业。

normal.en: The water rushed over the rocks.
normal.cn: 水从岩石上冲过。

normal.en: The rush hour starts at five.
normal.cn: 高峰时段五点开始。

normal.en: They rushed through lunch to catch the bus.
normal.cn: 他们匆匆吃完午饭去赶公交。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd pouring through a narrow gate.
abstract.cn: 想象人群从窄门涌出。

abstract.en: Imagine a river after heavy rain.
abstract.cn: 想象暴雨后的河水。

abstract.en: Think of a clock hand moving too fast.
abstract.cn: 想象钟表的指针转得太快。

examples.en: The crowd rushed toward the open doors.
examples.cn: 人群朝敞开的大门冲去。

examples.en: He rushed his speech and made mistakes.
examples.cn: 他讲得太仓促，出了错。

examples.en: The morning rush makes the roads slow.
examples.cn: 早高峰让道路变得缓慢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rush」读音像「如射」：像箭一样射出去，就是「冲、匆忙」。

core.cn: 核心意象：一股力量突然涌向某处。

definition_zh: 光滑的；顺利的；使平滑；变平静
definition_en: having an even surface, happening without problems, to make even, or to become calm
core_image: 一块被打磨得反光的木板
scene: 婴儿的皮肤像丝绸一样光滑。 The baby's skin is as smooth as silk.
sceneCN: 这里 smooth 是「光滑的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：婴儿的皮肤像丝绸一样光滑。

derivatives.zh: 顺利地
光滑；平稳
冰沙

senses.title: Even surface
senses.definition: having a surface that is even and not rough
senses.definitionCN: 表面平整而不粗糙
senses.example: The baby's skin is as smooth as silk.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿的皮肤像丝绸一样光滑。
senses.why: This is the physical texture sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是描述质感的义项。

senses.title: Without problems
senses.definition: happening without difficulties or sudden changes
senses.definitionCN: 没有困难或突变地发生
senses.example: We had a smooth journey home.
senses.exampleCN: 我们回家的旅程很顺利。
senses.why: An even surface suggests an easy path.
senses.whyCN: 平整的表面暗示顺畅的路径。

senses.title: Make even
senses.definition: to make a surface or situation even or calm
senses.definitionCN: 使表面或局面变得平整或平静
senses.example: She smoothed the cloth with her hand.
senses.exampleCN: 她用手把布抚平。
senses.why: The adjective became a verb of action.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转化为动作动词。

senses.title: Become calm
senses.definition: to become calm or less rough, used of water or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 指水面或情绪变得平静或缓和
senses.example: The sea smoothed after the storm.

normalIntro.en: Smooth means no roughness, no trouble, and no sudden movement.
normalIntro.cn: smooth 意味没有粗糙、没有麻烦、没有突变。

normal.en: The baby's skin is as smooth as silk.

normal.en: We had a smooth journey home.
normal.cn: 我们回家的旅程很顺利。

normal.en: She smoothed the cloth with her hand.

normal.en: He smoothed over the argument with a joke.

abstract.en: Patience smooths what force would break.
abstract.cn: 耐心能磨平蛮力会打碎的东西。

root: 由古英语 smoth（不粗糙的）演变而来，核心义「平整无碍」。

sensesIntro.en: Smooth means even, problem-free, to make even, or to become calm.
sensesIntro.cn: smooth 指平滑、顺利、使平整，或变平静。

core.en: Free from roughness or trouble.
core.cn: 没有粗糙或阻碍。

branches.en: Silk has no rough edge.

intro.en: Smooth builds words for texture, motion, and calm.
intro.cn: smooth 构成表示质感、运动和平静的词。

latinIntro.en: Smooth is a native English word, not Latin.

items.example: The smoothness of the floor surprised me.

definition_en: the way in which a word or a language is spoken, or a person's way of speaking
core_image: 一个词从纸上站起来，被嘴巴念成一段有重音、有长短的声音
scene: 语言课上，老师让学生把同一个单词读三遍，注意词尾那一点细微的差别。 Her pronunciation of the final consonant still sounded slightly French.
sceneCN: 这里取「读音、发音方式」的意思（第 1 个义项：一个词被说出来的声音形式）；句意为她对词尾辅音的读法仍带着一点法语味道。老师反复提醒的那个词尾就是线索。

derivatives.zh: 来自同一拉丁词干的动词，义为「发音；宣判」
在 pronunciation 前加表示「错误地」的前缀 mis-，义为「读错；错误发音」
由 pronounce 加 -able 与否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「念不出来的」

senses.title: The way a word or language is spoken
senses.definition: the way in which a particular word or language is spoken, including its sounds, stress and rhythm
senses.definitionCN: 某个词或某门语言被说出来的方式，包括音素、重音与节奏
senses.example: The dictionary gives two pronunciations for that word.
senses.exampleCN: 词典给这个词标了两种读音。
senses.why: The Latin noun pronuntiatio named the act of speaking out, and English borrowed that noun rather than the verb, so the word begins from the spoken form and not from the spelling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 pronuntiatio 本指「说出来的动作」，英语借的是这个名词而不是动词，所以这个词的起点是「说出来的声音形式」，不是纸上的拼写。

senses.title: A person's way of speaking
senses.definition: the way a particular person speaks, especially as a sign of where they grew up or learned the language
senses.definitionCN: 某个人说话的方式，尤指能看出其成长地或学语言经历的特征
senses.example: His pronunciation betrayed that he had grown up abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 他的口音暴露出他是在国外长大的。
senses.why: If the word names the sound of a whole language, it can also name the sound of one speaker, and in that shift it quietly takes over the work of the word accent.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能指整门语言的声音，也就能指某一个说话人的声音；在这一转之中，它悄悄接手了 accent 的工作。

senses.title: Speech sounds as a subject to teach
senses.definition: the part of language teaching that deals with sounds, stress and intonation
senses.definitionCN: 语言教学中处理音素、重音与语调的那一部分内容
senses.example: She teaches pronunciation to adult learners.
senses.exampleCN: 她给成年学员上语音课。
senses.why: Once the sounds of a language can be described, marked and corrected, they become something that can be taught, which is why the word also names a subject on a timetable.
senses.whyCN: 一门语言的声音一旦能被描述、标注、纠正，就成了可以教的东西，所以这个词也指课表上的一门内容。

intro.en: Pronunciation comes straight from a Latin action noun for speaking out, and that is the reason its spelling differs from the verb it seems to belong to.
intro.cn: pronunciation 直接来自一个表示「说出」的拉丁动作名词，这正是它的拼写与看似对应的动词不一致的原因。

items.en: Nuntiare meant to announce or report, and it supplied the announcing core of the whole family.
items.cn: nuntiare 意为宣告、报告，为整族词提供了「宣告」这个核心。

items.en: With the prefix pro-, forth, the verb pronuntiare meant to speak out, to utter sounds and to declare.
items.cn: 加上表示「向外」的前缀 pro-，动词 pronuntiare 意为说出、发声、宣告。

items.en: The noun pronuntiatio named the act and manner of speaking out, and its stem pronuntiat- is what English kept.
items.cn: 名词 pronuntiatio 指说出的动作与方式，英语保留的正是它的词干 pronuntiat-。

items.en: Old French passed the noun on as prononciation, turning the Latin t before i into a soft c sound.
items.cn: 古法语把名词写作 prononciation，拉丁语里 i 前的 t 变成了软音 c。

items.en: English fixed the spelling as pronunciation with n-u-n, following the Latin stem; the o of pronounce never entered, because this word came from the noun, not the verb.
items.cn: 英语按拉丁词干把拼写固定为带 n-u-n 的 pronunciation；pronounce 里的 o 从未进入，因为这个词来自名词而非动词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the Latin noun of speaking out; the near-meaning group gathers words about accent, clarity and the sound of speech.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「说出」名词上的形式；近义组收关于口音、清晰度与语音的词语。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to sound a word or to declare something.
entries.definitionCN: 表示读出一个词或宣布某事的动词。

entries.definition: A wrong way of saying a word.
entries.definitionCN: 读错的发音。

entries.definition: A formal public statement.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的公开声明。

entries.definition: An announcement, especially a solemn one.
entries.definitionCN: 宣告，尤指庄重的宣告。

entries.definition: The way people from a place or group speak.
entries.definitionCN: 某地或某群体说话的腔调。

entries.definition: The clear production of speech sounds.
entries.definitionCN: 语音的清晰发出。

entries.definition: The clarity with which words are spoken or sung.
entries.definitionCN: 说话或演唱时咬字的清晰程度。

entries.definition: The rise and fall of the voice in speech.
