normalIntro.en: The word is a mouth shaping a word into sound, and its memories sit on the Latin noun, on stress, and on the missing letter.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一张嘴把一个词念成声音，记忆点落在拉丁名词、重音，以及那个消失的字母上。

normal.en: The verb has an o after the n and the noun does not, because the noun came from Latin pronuntiatio while the verb came through French prononcier.
normal.cn: 动词在 n 后面有 o，名词没有，因为名词来自拉丁语 pronuntiatio，动词则经法语 prononcier 传来。

normal.en: The -tion ending marks a noun of action, exactly as in declaration and explanation.
normal.cn: -tion 结尾标明这是一个动作名词，就像 declaration 与 explanation 一样。

normal.en: Stress falls late, on the syllable that carries -ation, so the first syllables stay light and quick.
normal.cn: 重音落在后面带 -ation 的音节上，前面几个音节因此又轻又快。

normal.en: Mispronunciation adds mis-, wrongly, and keeps the full Latin stem, so the n-u-n stays visible.
normal.cn: mispronunciation 加上表示「错误地」的 mis-，并保留完整的拉丁词干，所以 n-u-n 清楚可见。

normal.en: Annunciation and announce share the announcing root, so this family is not only about mouths.
normal.cn: annunciation 与 announce 共享「宣告」词根，可见这一族词并不只关乎嘴。

abstract.en: Pronunciation is the part of a word that a dictionary can only approximate; the mouth always finishes the job.
abstract.cn: 发音是词典只能大致描摹的那一部分，最后的成品总要由嘴巴完成。

abstract.en: A word can be spelled one way and spoken another, and the gap between the noun and the verb is a small monument to that fact.
abstract.cn: 词可以这样写、那样念，名词与动词之间的那点差别，正是这件事留下的一个小纪念碑。

abstract.en: To judge someone by their pronunciation is to hear history, geography and family gathered into a single vowel.
abstract.cn: 凭发音判断一个人，等于从一个元音里听出历史、地理与家庭。

examples.en: The dictionary gives two pronunciations for that word.
examples.cn: 词典给这个词标了两种读音。

examples.en: His pronunciation betrayed that he had grown up abroad.
examples.cn: 他的口音暴露出他是在国外长大的。

examples.en: She teaches pronunciation to adult learners.
examples.cn: 她给成年学员上语音课。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若难西」——念着就觉得有点难，越难越要练，正是发音。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向外）+ nuntiare（宣告）构成 pronuntiare，其动作名词 pronuntiatio（说出、宣告）经古法语 prononciation 进入英语；词干保留 n-u-n，所以拼写里没有 pronounce 的 o。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the spoken shape of a word; the senses divide into the sound of a word, the sound of a speaker, and the sound of a language as something to be taught.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「一个词被说出来的声音形状」；义项分成一个词的读音、一个说话人的口音，以及作为教学对象的一门语言的语音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a printed word lifted off the page and shaped by the mouth into a stretch of sound with its own beat.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个印在纸上的词脱离纸面，被嘴巴塑造成一段有自己节拍的声音。

branches.en: two pronunciations printed side by side in a dictionary
branches.cn: 词典里并排印出的两种读音

branches.en: a familiar word said in an unfamiliar voice
branches.cn: 熟悉词被陌生嗓音读出

branches.en: a listener guessing where a stranger grew up
branches.cn: 听者猜陌生人是在哪里长大的

branches.en: a classroom drilling one difficult consonant
branches.cn: 课堂上反复练一个难辅音

branches.en: a recording played again to catch a single sound
branches.cn: 为听清一个音再放一遍录音

intro.en: A Latin verb of announcing and the action noun built from it hold the word together; French softened the consonants and English kept the Latin stem in the spelling.
intro.cn: 表示宣告的拉丁语动词及其动作名词共同支撑这个词；法语软化了辅音，英语则在拼写上保留了拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin nuntiare, to announce, its compound pronuntiare, and the action noun pronuntiatio are the direct sources of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nuntiare（宣告）、其复合形式 pronuntiare 以及动作名词 pronuntiatio 是英语这个词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 按；压；敦促；报刊；新闻界；出版社；榨取
definition_en: to push something firmly; to urge someone strongly; also newspapers and the people who produce them, a publishing house, or the act of squeezing juice or oil out
core_image: 一只手把按钮按到底，塑料外壳微微下陷，灯随即亮起
scene: 楼道里很暗，他伸出一根手指朝墙上的开关按下去，灯立刻亮起，脚步声也停了。 Press the button twice if the door does not open.
sceneCN: 这里 press 指「按、压」（第 1 个义项：用手或工具对某物施加压力）；句意为如果门没开就按两次按钮。图中可辨识物件：墙上的开关、手指、走廊的灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 press 加名词后缀 -ure 构成，义为「压力」
由 press 加 -ing 构成，义为「紧迫的；迫切的」
由 pressure 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「加压；密封加压」

senses.title: To push something firmly
senses.definition: to push steadily on something with the hand or a tool
senses.definitionCN: 用手或工具持续对某物施加推力
senses.example: Press the green button to start the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 按下绿色按钮启动机器。
senses.why: The Latin verb premere simply meant to press, and this physical push is the sense from which every other use of the word can be traced.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 premere 本义就是「压」，用手施加推力的这个动作是整个词义树的根，后面所有引申都能从这一下按压找到起点。

senses.title: To urge someone strongly
senses.definition: to try hard to persuade someone to do something, especially by repeating the request
senses.definitionCN: 反复请求以努力说服某人做某事
senses.example: The union pressed the government for a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 工会敦促政府给出答复。
senses.why: Pressure applied to a person rather than an object becomes insistence, so the same verb moves from pushing a surface to pushing a decision forward.
senses.whyCN: 把压力从物体转到人身上，就变成了「不断施压、要求答复」，按压的动作没有变，只是受力的对象从按钮变成了决策者，因此产生「敦促」这一义。

senses.title: Newspapers and the people who make them
senses.definition: newspapers and magazines as a group, together with the journalists who work for them
senses.definitionCN: 报纸与杂志这一整体，以及为其工作的记者
senses.example: The story was widely reported in the press.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事在新闻界被广泛报道。
senses.why: When printing presses made daily papers possible, the machine that pressed ink onto paper gave its name to the papers themselves and then to the whole profession.
senses.whyCN: 印刷机让日报成为可能，把油墨压到纸上的那台机器就用 press 来称呼，随后这个词从机器转到印出来的报纸，再扩指整个新闻行业。

senses.title: A publishing house
senses.definition: a company that prints and publishes books, or the business of publishing
senses.definitionCN: 印刷并出版书籍的公司，或出版这一行业
senses.example: The book came out under a small university press.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书由一家小型大学出版社出版。
senses.why: The same machine also names the firm that owns it, so press shifts from the equipment to the business that turns manuscripts into bound books.
senses.whyCN: 同一台机器也能代指拥有它的机构，于是 press 从设备滑向企业，用来指把书稿变成成书的出版社，这一义项至今保留在大学社名与出版品牌里。

senses.title: To squeeze out liquid
senses.definition: to squeeze fruit, seeds, or oil to get the liquid inside
senses.definitionCN: 挤压果实、种子或油料以取得其中的液体
senses.example: They press the olives within a day of picking.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在采摘当天就把橄榄榨成油。
senses.why: Squeezing olives is the most literal kind of pressing, force applied until something flows out, and it survives beside the abstract senses.
senses.whyCN: 榨橄榄是最字面的一种「压」：一直加力，直到有东西流出来；这个用法与引申义长期并存，说明表示压力的词始终保留着「压出液体」的具体一面。

intro.en: Press comes from a Latin verb for pressing; a repeated-action form of it reached French and then English, and the printing machine later pushed the word into newspapers and publishing.
intro.cn: press 来自表示「压」的拉丁动词；它的反复体形式经法语进入英语，后来印刷机又把这个词推进报刊与出版领域。

items.en: The verb premere meant to press, squeeze, or push down, and it is the base of a large family of English words.
items.cn: 动词 premere 意为压、挤、向下推，是一大批英语词的共同基础。

items.en: A frequentative form pressare described pressing again and again, and this is the branch that travelled into French.
items.cn: pressare 是反复体形式，表示「一再压」，进入法语的正是这一支。

items.en: Old French presser kept both the physical sense and the sense of urging someone, and English borrowed it as pressen.
items.cn: 古法语 presser 同时保留「压」的具体义与「催促某人」的引申义，英语借入后写作 pressen。

items.en: Middle English press covered pushing, crowding, and the machine that pressed ink onto paper.
items.cn: 中古英语的 press 覆盖推、挤，以及把油墨压到纸上的机器。

items.en: Modern English lets the noun name the machine, the newspapers it produces, the publishing house, and the journalists as a body.
items.cn: 现代英语让这个名词同时指机器、机器印出的报纸、出版社，以及作为群体的新闻工作者。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin root for pressing and its English compounds; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of force and words for the news industry.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「压」的拉丁词根及其英语复合词展开；近义组收施加力量的动词与新闻行业的说法。

entries.definition: A steady force acting on a surface, or strong influence on a person.
entries.definitionCN: 持续作用在表面上的力；对人所施的压力。

entries.definition: Needing attention right away.
entries.definitionCN: 需要立刻处理的；紧迫的。

entries.definition: To press things together into a smaller space.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西压到一起，使其占更小空间。

entries.definition: To put a thought into words, or to send something fast.
entries.definitionCN: 把想法说出来；快速送出。

entries.definition: To move something away by force.
entries.definitionCN: 用力把某物推开。

entries.definition: To press something from both sides.
entries.definitionCN: 从两侧挤压某物。

entries.definition: Newspapers, television, and other channels of news.
entries.definitionCN: 报纸、电视等新闻传播渠道。

entries.definition: To ask strongly that something be done.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈要求做某事。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of pressing plus its repeated form; the family spreads from physical force to urging people and to printing words on paper.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是表示「压」的拉丁动词及其反复体；词族从物理的力，扩展到催促人，再扩展到把字印到纸上。

normal.en: Press comes from Latin premere, to press, and its frequentative pressare gave the French verb that English borrowed.
normal.cn: press 来自拉丁语 premere（压），它的反复体 pressare 生出法语动词，再传入英语。

normal.en: Pressure is press plus -ure, the result of pressing: a force that keeps acting on a surface.
normal.cn: pressure 是 press 加 -ure，指压出来的结果：持续作用在表面上的力。

normal.en: Compress and express both keep the Latin root premere, one pressing things together, the other pressing ideas out.
normal.cn: compress 与 express 都保留拉丁词根 premere：一个把东西压到一起，一个把想法压出来。

normal.en: The printing press pressed ink into paper, and from that machine came the sense newspapers and journalists.
normal.cn: 印刷机把油墨压进纸里，而「报刊、记者」这一义正是从那台机器来的。

normal.en: Pressing as an adjective keeps the physical weight: a pressing problem is one that bears down on you now.
normal.cn: 形容词 pressing 保留了物理上的重量：a pressing problem 就是此刻压在你身上的问题。

abstract.en: Press is what force looks like when it has a direction: down on a button, out through an olive, or straight at a person who must answer.
abstract.cn: press 就是力有了方向之后的样子：向下按按钮，向外榨橄榄，或直直压向一个必须答复的人。

abstract.en: One machine that pushed ink into paper was enough to rename an entire profession.
abstract.cn: 一台把油墨压进纸里的机器，就足以给整个行业改名。

abstract.en: The word shows that persuasion and printing are both forms of applied pressure, one on people and one on surfaces.
abstract.cn: 这个词说明说服与印刷都是「加压力」的形式：一个作用在人身上，一个作用在表面上。

examples.en: Press the green button to start the machine.
examples.cn: 按下绿色按钮启动机器。

examples.en: The story was widely reported in the press.
examples.cn: 这件事在新闻界被广泛报道。

examples.en: She pressed the olives by hand.
examples.cn: 她用手把橄榄榨成油。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普雷斯」——手掌往下一「压」，就是 press；压出来的报纸也叫 press。谐音只助记。

root: 拉丁语 premere（压）→ 反复体 pressare（一再压）→ 古法语 presser → 中古英语 pressen → 英语 press；从「按压」引申出「施压敦促」，再由印刷机引申出「报刊、新闻界、出版社」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is downward force; the senses divide into physical pressing, pressure on people, squeezing out liquid, and the printing machine with everything it produced.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是向下的力；义项由此分为物理按压、对人施压、榨出液体，以及印刷机及其产物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger driving a button to its stop until the lamp answers with light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指把按钮按到底，灯以亮起作为回应。

branches.en: a finger sinking a button to its stop
olive oil running into a jar
a repeated request left on a desk
a folded newspaper on a breakfast table
a colophon on the last page of a book

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of pressing, its repeated form, the French verb taken from it, and the English endings that name the force and the action.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「压」的拉丁动词、其反复体、由它而来的法语动词，以及命名压力与动作的英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a steady force on a surface
a machine that prints on paper

definition_en: the quality that makes things red, blue, yellow and so on; also a verb meaning to add colour
core_image: 让世界不再灰白的红黄蓝
scene: 美术课上，同学们用蜡笔给春天的图画涂色。 Let us colour the flowers in the picture.
sceneCN: 这里 colour 是动词「涂色」（第 3 个义项：给图画上颜色）；句意是给画里的花涂色。

derivatives.zh: 由 colour 加 -ful 构成，义为「多彩的；鲜艳的」
由 colour 加 -less 构成，义为「无色的；乏味的」
由 dis- 加 colour 构成，义为「使变色；褪色」
美式拼写，义为「颜色」

senses.title: Red, blue, yellow and the like
senses.definition: the appearance of things that makes them look red, blue, green and so on
senses.definitionCN: 使物体呈现红、蓝、绿等外观的性质
senses.example: What is your favourite colour at school?
senses.exampleCN: 在学校你最喜欢什么颜色？
senses.why: Light of different waves paints the world, and the look it gives is colour.
senses.whyCN: 不同波长的光给世界涂上外观，这个外观就是颜色。

senses.title: Paint or pigment
senses.definition: a substance you put on a surface to give it colour
senses.definitionCN: 涂在物体表面让它变色的物质
senses.example: Buy some colours for the art class.
senses.exampleCN: 为美术课买些颜料。
senses.why: The look can be kept in a tube, so the substance took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 这种外观能装进管子里保存，物质便借用了同一个名字。

senses.title: To add colour to something
senses.definition: to put colour on something with pencils, paint or markers
senses.definitionCN: 用铅笔、颜料或彩笔给东西上色
senses.example: Colour the sky blue in your drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 把画里的天空涂成蓝色。
senses.why: The noun moved into a verb the way many English nouns do.
senses.whyCN: 英语名词常直接转作动词，colour 也是如此。

senses.title: The healthy pink of the face
senses.definition: the natural red of someone's cheeks showing health
senses.definitionCN: 脸颊上显出健康的红色
senses.example: After the run, her face regained colour.
senses.exampleCN: 跑完步，她脸上恢复了血色。
senses.why: Colour shows life on a face as paint shows colour on a wall.
senses.whyCN: 颜料显色于墙，血色显色于脸，词义便这样迁移。

intro.en: Colour goes back to Latin words about covering and skin.
intro.cn: colour 可以追溯到拉丁语里表示「覆盖」「皮肤」的词。

items.en: Latin color meant colour or complexion; many link it to celare, to hide, as colour covers the surface.
items.cn: 拉丁语 color 指颜色、肤色；许多人把它与 celare（遮盖）相联系，因为颜色覆盖了表面。

items.en: Latin colorare meant to colour or give complexion.
items.cn: 拉丁语 colorare 意为着色、赋予肤色。

items.en: Old French colour carried the word into England.
items.cn: 古法语 colour 把这个词带进了英格兰。

items.en: Middle English colour meant both look and paint.
items.cn: 中古英语 colour 兼指外观与颜料。

items.en: Modern English kept colour in Britain and shortened it to color in the US.
items.cn: 现代英语英式保留 colour，美式简写为 color。

note.en: The first group collects words close in spelling; the second collects kinds of colour.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写相近的词，第二组收与颜色相关的词。

entries.definition: The part of a shirt round the neck.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「衣领」，与 colour 拼写相近但词源不同。

entries.definition: The American spelling of colour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「颜色」，是 colour 的美式拼法。

entries.definition: Great fame or honour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「荣耀」，形近但词源不同。

entries.definition: Coloured liquid put on a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「油漆；颜料」，与颜料义相近。

entries.definition: A substance giving colour to things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「色素；颜料」，较专业的说法。

entries.definition: A slight shade of a colour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「色调；淡色」。

normalIntro.en: Remember colour through the rainbow and the US spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 从彩虹与美式拼写两个角度记 colour。

normal.en: The US spelling color drops a u.
normal.cn: 美式拼写 color 少一个 u。

normal.en: Rainbows show seven colours.
normal.cn: 彩虹有七种颜色。

normal.en: colour and collar differ by one middle letter.
normal.cn: colour 与 collar 中间字母不同。

normal.en: colour pencils are used in art class.
normal.cn: 美术课用彩色铅笔。

normal.en: A colourful painting has many colours.
normal.cn: 多彩的画里颜色很多。

abstract.en: Picture a grey world suddenly painted bright.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色世界突然被涂亮。

abstract.en: See a brush dipping into a tube of red.
abstract.cn: 想象画笔蘸进一管红色。

abstract.en: Feel warm red rising into tired cheeks.
abstract.cn: 感觉红色回到疲惫的脸颊。

examples.en: Autumn gives the park beautiful colours.
examples.cn: 秋天给公园披上美丽的颜色。

examples.en: Please colour the tree green and the sun yellow.
examples.cn: 请把树涂成绿色、太阳涂成黄色。

examples.en: His face lost colour when he heard the news.
examples.cn: 听到消息后，他的脸失去了血色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡勒」——蜡笔一按「卡勒」一声，颜色就涂上了，colour 就是颜色。

root: 拉丁语 color（颜色）→ colorare（着色）→ 古法语 colour → 中古英语 colour → 现代英语 colour（英式），美式拼作 color；同族词有 colourful（多彩的）、discolour（褪色）。

sensesIntro.en: Colour covers the look of light, the paint in tubes, the act of colouring and even the pink of cheeks.
sensesIntro.cn: colour 涵盖光的颜色、管中颜料、涂色动作，甚至脸颊血色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the paint that covers a grey world
core.cn: 核心意象：让灰白世界变鲜艳的涂料

branches.en: Red, blue and the rainbow
Tubes in the art room
Colouring pictures in class
Pink cheeks after running
Bright colours in daily life

intro.en: Colour builds a family of bright words.
intro.cn: colour 衍生出一族与色彩有关的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root color means colour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 color 意为颜色。

items.example: The stage was colourful and bright.
items.exampleCN: 舞台五彩缤纷、明亮夺目。

items.meaning: to change colour in a bad way

items.example: The poster says color in the US.
His face turned pale with fear.
Which shade of blue do you like?
items.exampleCN: 你喜欢哪种色调的蓝色？

items.example: A rainbow appeared after the rain.

definition_en: a thing known to be true, or something that has actually happened
core_image: 钉在墙上的证据板：每张卡片都是一件已发生过的事，风吹不走
scene: 辩论课前，老师要求每人先核对自己的资料来源，再上台发言。 Before the debate, check that every statement in your notes is a fact.
sceneCN: 这里指「已知为真之事」，对应第 1 个义项：可被证明为真的信息；句意为辩论前确认笔记中每条陈述都是事实。画面要点：资料卡、勾选的笔迹、辩论台。

derivatives.zh: 事实的（基础词加形容词后缀，指以事实为准）
事实上（形容词加副词后缀）
实情调查的（复合形容词，指查明事实的）
工厂（词根 fac「做」加名词后缀，指「做东西的地方」）
因素；因子（词根 fac「做」加者缀，指起作用的东西）

senses.title: Something known to be true
senses.definition: a piece of information that can be shown to be true
senses.definitionCN: 能够被证明为真实的信息
senses.example: The report is based on facts.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告以事实为依据。
senses.why: A deed done leaves evidence; what has truly happened becomes what is known.
senses.whyCN: 做过的事留下证据；真实发生者即已知之事。

senses.title: Truth as opposed to invention
senses.definition: reality rather than imagination or opinion
senses.definitionCN: 实在，而非想象或意见
senses.example: Separate fact from fiction.
senses.exampleCN: 区分事实与虚构。
senses.why: Done deeds are the hard ground under words; fiction floats above it.
senses.whyCN: 已做之事是言语下的硬地；虚构悬于其上。

senses.title: An event or deed
senses.definition: something that has actually happened
senses.definitionCN: 实际发生过的事情
senses.example: The facts of the case are clear.
senses.exampleCN: 案情事实清楚。
senses.why: The oldest Latin sense of factum was the act itself, not the knowledge of it.
senses.whyCN: factum 在拉丁语中最古老的含义就是行为本身，而非对它的认知。

senses.title: A detail used in argument
senses.definition: one item of information used to support a claim
senses.definitionCN: 用于支撑论点的一条信息
senses.example: Give me one fact to prove it.
senses.exampleCN: 给我一个事实来证明。
senses.why: Argument is built from confirmed happenings, one stone at a time.
senses.whyCN: 论证由确证之事一块块垒成。

intro.en: Fact descends from Latin factum, 'a thing done', the past participle of facere, 'to do'.
intro.cn: fact 源自拉丁语 factum（已做成的事），即 facere（做）的过去分词。

items.en: Latin facere meant to do or make; its participle factum named a deed, a thing done.
items.cn: 拉丁语 facere 意为做、造；其分词 factum 指已做之事、行为。

items.en: Medieval Latin used factum for an event or deed recorded in documents.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用 factum 指文献中记录的事件或行为。

items.en: Old French fact and fait passed the word on with the sense of an act and its record.
items.cn: 古法语 fact、fait 把「行为及其记录」之义传了下去。

items.en: Middle English took fact in the sixteenth century mainly for a thing known to have happened.
items.cn: 中古英语在十六世纪借入 fact，主要指确已发生之事。

items.en: Modern English widened fact to any verifiable statement, giving in fact, in point of fact.
items.cn: 现代英语把 fact 扩展为一切可核验的陈述，并出现 in fact、in point of fact。

note.en: Look-alikes share the Latin root fac- or spelling; near-meaning words name kinds of truth and reality.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 fac- 或拼写；近义组命名各种「真实与事实」。

entries.definition: the Latin root to do or make, seen in factory and factor
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁词根「做」，见于 factory、factor

entries.definition: a mistake or weakness
entries.definitionCN: 过错；拼写相近但源自拉丁 fallere「欺骗」

entries.definition: a thing done
entries.definitionCN: 行为；与 fact 相差一字母，且语义同源但词形不同

entries.definition: the state of being true
entries.definitionCN: 真实性；真相

entries.definition: things as they actually are
entries.definitionCN: 实际存在的事物

entries.definition: a single piece of given information
entries.definitionCN: 一条给定的信息

normalIntro.en: Five grips on a word that means a thing already done.
normalIntro.cn: 意为「已做成之事」的词，五个抓手。

normal.en: Latin facere means to do, and factum the thing done, so a fact is what has been done.
normal.cn: 拉丁 facere＝做；factum＝做成了的，所以 fact 就是既成之事。

normal.en: in fact is the highest-frequency emphasis phrase in spoken English.
normal.cn: in fact 是口语最高频的强调短语。

normal.en: factory shares the root: a place where things are done or made.
normal.cn: factory 与 fact 同根：都来自「做」。

normal.en: as a matter of fact sounds a step more formal than in fact.
normal.cn: as a matter of fact 语气比 in fact 更正式。

normal.en: fact and fault differ by one letter: doing right makes a fact, doing wrong a fault.
normal.cn: fact 与 fault 只差字母：做对是事实，做错是过失。

abstract.en: Facts are floor tiles: opinions stand firm only when laid on them.
abstract.cn: 事实像地砖，观点只能铺在地砖上才稳。

abstract.en: Every finished deed is a full stop that cannot be rewritten.
abstract.cn: 每件已完成的事都是一个不再改变的句号。

abstract.en: Truth is a jigsaw puzzle and facts are the pieces; only all of them show the picture.
abstract.cn: 真相是拼图，facts 是碎片，全找齐才见整图。

examples.en: In fact, the bridge opened two years ahead of schedule.
examples.cn: 事实上，大桥提前两年通车。

examples.en: The article mixes fact with speculation.
examples.cn: 这篇文章把事实与猜测混在一起。

examples.en: History books record the facts of the period, not the rumours.
examples.cn: 史书记录那个时代的事实，而非传言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法克特」——法律可证之「特」殊之事，就是事实。

root: 拉丁语 facere（做）的过去分词 factum（已做成之事）经中世纪拉丁语与古法语 fact/fait 进入英语。同根词族广大：factory（做的场所）、factor（起作用者）、manufacture（手工做）。

sensesIntro.en: From a deed done outward to known truth, reality, and pieces of evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「已做之事」扩展到已知真相、实在与证据条目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thing already done, standing there as evidence.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件已经做完、站在那里作证的事。

branches.en: THE KNOWN: information shown to be true.
branches.cn: 已知之事：被证明为真的信息。

branches.en: THE REAL: truth against invention.
branches.cn: 实在：与虚构相对的真实。

branches.en: THE HAPPENED: the event itself.
THE EVIDENCE: details supporting claims.
THE RECORD: facts kept in writing.

intro.en: Fact is a naked piece of the Latin verb facere; the whole fac- family is around it.
intro.cn: fact 是拉丁动词 facere 裸露的一块；整个 fac- 词族围绕它。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere, to do or make, seeds a huge word family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere（做、造）孕育了庞大的词族。

items.example: fact and factory share this root

items.meaning: the one who or that which does
a place where something is done
a small group that acts together
items.exampleCN: 一个政治派别分裂出去

items.example: the library owes much to its benefactor

latinEntries.meaning: a making, a group that acts

definition_en: to work or function, to control a machine, to run a business, or to perform a medical operation
core_image: 一只手按下按钮，整排机器依次发出低响，像身体里某处重新开始供血
scene: 深夜的泵房里，值班员按下启动键，旧水泵先抖了两下，随后平稳地响了起来。 The old pump began to operate smoothly after the valve was replaced.
sceneCN: 这里是「运转」（第 1 个义项：机器或系统开始工作并保持运行）；句意为换过阀门之后，旧水泵开始平稳运转。图中可辨识物件：泵房管道、启动键、压力表。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语过去分词词干加 -tion 构成，义为「操作；手术；运算」
由拉丁语 operator（干活的人）进入英语，义为「操作员；运算符」
由 operari 加 -ive 构成，义为「起作用的；实施中的」

senses.title: To work or run
senses.definition: to work or function, especially of a machine, system or service
senses.definitionCN: 尤指机器、系统或服务在工作、起作用
senses.example: The heating system operates at low cost in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这套供暖系统冬天运行成本很低。
senses.why: Latin operari means to work, so a machine that runs is the old idea of working moved from a person onto a device.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 operari 意为「干活」，机器在运行这个义项，就是把「干活」从人身上挪到了装置上。

senses.title: To control a machine
senses.definition: to control or use a machine, vehicle or piece of equipment
senses.definitionCN: 控制并使用机器、车辆或设备
senses.example: Only trained staff may operate the crane.
senses.exampleCN: 只有受过训练的人员才能操作这台起重机。
senses.why: If a machine can work by itself, a person can also make it work, and the transitive use simply adds a hand on the controls.
senses.whyCN: 机器既然能自己运行，人也能使它运行；及物用法只是在「干活」这件事上多了一只放在操纵杆上的手。

senses.title: To perform surgery
senses.definition: to cut into a patient's body in order to treat a disease or an injury
senses.definitionCN: 切开病人身体以治疗疾病或损伤
senses.example: Surgeons operated on her knee at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生在黎明时为她做了膝关节手术。
senses.why: Surgery is skilled work done with the hands on the body, so the general verb for working took the medical sense through the phrase operate on.
senses.whyCN: 手术是靠双手在身体上完成的技艺活，于是「干活」这个泛用动词借着 operate on 这个说法，担起了医学含义。

senses.title: To run a business or organization
senses.definition: to manage or run a business, service or organization
senses.definitionCN: 管理或经营一项生意、服务或组织
senses.example: The charity operates three shelters in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构在市内经营三家收容所。
senses.why: Running an organization is continuous work, so the same verb moves from a single machine to a whole enterprise.
senses.whyCN: 经营一个组织是持续不断的活，同一个动词就这样从一台机器扩大到整个机构。

intro.en: Operate comes straight from Latin, where a verb for working gave English both the verb and its nouns; it is not the same word as opera, which arrived through Italian.
intro.cn: operate 直接从拉丁语进入英语，那里一个意为「干活」的动词为英语提供了动词和它的名词；它与经意大利语而来的 opera 不是同一个词。

items.en: Latin opus named work or a product, and its genitive operis supplied the stem for the verbs of working.
items.cn: 拉丁语 opus 指工作或成果，属格 operis 为表示「干活」的一系列动词提供了词干。

items.en: Operari was a deponent verb meaning to work, to labor or to produce an effect.
items.cn: operari 是一个异态动词，意为干活、劳作或产生作用。

items.en: Its past participle operatus meant having worked, and this is the form English took when it borrowed the verb.
items.cn: 它的过去分词 operatus 意为「已经干过」，英语借入动词时带的就是这个形式。

items.en: Early English operate meant to produce an effect or to exert force, a sense still heard in the word operation.
items.cn: 早期的英语 operate 意为产生效果或施加力量，这层意思至今还能在 operation 里听到。

items.en: Modern English widened operate to machines, businesses and surgery while keeping the older sense of having an effect.
items.cn: 现代英语把 operate 扩展到机器、企业和手术，同时保留了「起作用」这层旧义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the Latin-derived working family; the near-meaning group is everyday verbs for running or handling something.
note.cn: 形近组是由拉丁语「干活」长出的词族；近义组是日常里表示运转或摆弄某物的动词。

entries.definition: The act of working, or a medical procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 运作的行为，或医疗手术。

entries.definition: Working, or used for working, as in an operating system.
entries.definitionCN: 运转的或用于运转的，如操作系统。

entries.definition: A person who works a machine or handles telephone calls.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机器或处理电话的人。

entries.definition: Working or in force, and also a person who carries out secret work.
entries.definitionCN: 起作用的、实施中的，也指从事秘密工作的人。

entries.definition: To make a machine or a business work.
entries.definitionCN: 使机器或企业运转。

entries.definition: To work in the normal or expected way.
entries.definitionCN: 以正常或预期的方式工作。

entries.definition: To use or control something with the hands.
entries.definitionCN: 用手使用或控制某物。

normalIntro.en: Everything in this family goes back to the Latin verb for working, so the mnemonics follow the work from hands to machines to bodies.
normalIntro.cn: 这一族词都可追到拉丁语表示「干活」的动词，所以联想沿着「活」从双手走到机器，再到身体。

normal.en: Operari means to work, so operate is first of all to be busy doing something.
normal.cn: operari 意为干活，所以 operate 首先是「在忙着做某事」。

normal.en: Operation adds -tion and turns the working into a thing you can name.
normal.cn: operation 加 -tion，把「干活」变成一个可以叫出名字的东西。

normal.en: Operator adds -or and turns the working into the person who does it.
normal.cn: operator 加 -or，把「干活」变成干活的那个人。

normal.en: Operate on is the medical phrase, where the body is the thing being worked on.
normal.cn: operate on 是医学说法，被「干活」的对象就是身体。

normal.en: Operative means still at work, which is why a spy is also called one.
normal.cn: operative 意为仍在起作用，这就是特工也被叫作 operative 的原因。

abstract.en: A hand on a lever is the shortest picture of operate: effort passing into a machine.
abstract.cn: 一只手搭在操纵杆上，就是 operate 最短的画面：力气传进机器。

abstract.en: A machine that runs is a person's work continuing after the person has stepped away.
abstract.cn: 机器自己转着，就是人的活在离开之后还继续着。

abstract.en: Cutting a body to mend it shows how far the plain word for working can travel.
abstract.cn: 切开身体去修补它，说明「干活」这个平常词能走多远。

examples.en: The old pump began to operate smoothly after the valve was replaced.
examples.cn: 换过阀门之后，旧水泵开始平稳运转。

examples.en: Only trained staff may operate the crane.
examples.cn: 只有受过训练的人员才能操作这台起重机。

examples.en: The charity operates three shelters in the city.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构在市内经营三家收容所。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，怕累他」——机器开动以后，最怕累坏那个守着它的人；记住 operate 是操作、运转。

root: 拉丁语 opus（工作、成果）派生动词 operari（干活、起作用），过去分词 operatus 进入英语成为 operate；同族词有 operation、operator、operative、operating。opera 虽与它共享更远的拉丁词根，却经意大利语而来、指「歌剧」，不能与 operate 混用。

sensesIntro.en: The core is work being done; the senses move from a machine running, to a hand controlling it, to surgery, and finally to running a whole enterprise.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「正在干的活」；义项从机器自己运行，移到人伸手操纵，再到在身体上动刀，最后到经营整个机构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing a button and a row of machines answering with a low hum.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按下按钮，一排机器用低沉的声音回应。

branches.en: a pump finding its rhythm after a repair
branches.cn: 修好之后水泵重新找到节奏

branches.en: an operator guiding a crane over a roof
branches.cn: 操作员把起重机吊过屋顶

branches.en: a trainee learning to keep both hands still
branches.cn: 学徒练习让两只手保持不动

branches.en: a lamp above a table in a quiet room
branches.cn: 安静房间里，台面上方的一盏灯

branches.en: a small office counting the shelters it runs
branches.cn: 小办公室清点自己经营的那几家收容所

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle turned English verb, and the family adds -tion for the act, -or for the person and -ive for the working quality.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语分词变成的英语动词；同族词用 -tion 表示行为，用 -or 表示人，用 -ive 表示「起作用的」性质。

latinIntro.en: The Latin behind operate is the working branch of the opus family: the verb, its participle and the agent noun.
latinIntro.cn: operate 背后的拉丁语是 opus 一族里「干活」的那一支：动词、分词和施事名词。

definition_en: the systematic study of the physical world, the knowledge gained from it, or a particular field of such study
core_image: 实验室里，试管排成一列，屏幕上跳动着刚记录的数据
scene: 他翻开课本，想弄明白实验背后的道理。 Science explains how the experiment works.
sceneCN: 这里 science 是「科学」（第 1 个义项）；句意：科学解释了实验如何运作。

derivatives.zh: 科学的
科学家
科学地
科幻小说

senses.title: Systematic knowledge
senses.definition: the organized study of the physical world through observation and experiment
senses.definitionCN: 通过观察和实验对物质世界进行的有系统研究
senses.example: Science has changed daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 科学改变了日常生活。
senses.why: The central sense is organized knowledge of nature.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是关于自然的有组织知识。

senses.title: Scientific activity
senses.definition: the work of doing scientific research
senses.definitionCN: 进行科学研究的工作
senses.example: Science needs patience and honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 科学研究需要耐心与诚实。
senses.why: The knowledge sense extends to the activity that produces it.
senses.whyCN: 知识义延伸到产生知识的研究活动。

senses.title: A field of study
senses.definition: a particular branch of systematic study
senses.definitionCN: 系统研究的某个分支
senses.example: She studies computer science.
senses.exampleCN: 她学习计算机科学。
senses.why: A broad method narrows to one named discipline.
senses.whyCN: 宽泛的方法缩小为一个具体学科。

intro.en: Science comes from Latin scientia, knowledge, from scire, to know.
intro.cn: science 源自拉丁语 scientia（知识），来自 scire（知道）。

items.en: Scire meant to know.
items.cn: scire 意为知道。

items.en: Scientia meant knowledge or understanding.
items.cn: scientia 意为知识或理解。

items.en: Science meant knowledge of any kind.
items.cn: science 意为任何类型的知识。

items.en: Science narrowed to knowledge based on observation.
items.cn: science 缩小为基于观察的知识。

items.en: Science now names the study of the natural world.
items.cn: 现代英语中 science 指对自然世界的研究。

note.en: Science is compared with similar-looking words and with words for knowledge and study.
note.cn: 把 science 与形近词以及表示知识与研究的词作比较。

entries.definition: complete quiet
entries.definitionCN: 寂静

entries.definition: a sense of right and wrong
entries.definitionCN: 良心

entries.definition: a smell
entries.definitionCN: 气味

entries.definition: information and understanding
entries.definitionCN: 知识

entries.definition: careful study to find facts
entries.definitionCN: 研究

entries.definition: a field of academic study
entries.definitionCN: 学科

normalIntro.en: Science is knowledge, scientific is the adjective, and scientist is the person.
normalIntro.cn: science 是知识，scientific 是形容词，scientist 是人。

normal.en: Science fiction mixes science with imagination.
normal.cn: 科幻小说把科学与想象结合。

normal.en: Computer science is the study of computing.
normal.cn: 计算机科学是研究计算的学科。

normal.en: A science lab is where experiments happen.
normal.cn: 科学实验室是做实验的地方。

normal.en: Science and scientist share the same base.
normal.cn: science 与 scientist 同根。

normal.en: The ence ending marks a noun.
normal.cn: ence 结尾提示这是名词。

abstract.en: Science began as knowledge in general, then narrowed to tested knowledge.
abstract.cn: science 起初泛指知识，后来缩小为经过检验的知识。

abstract.en: The word links a method, a body of knowledge, and a field.
abstract.cn: 这个词连接方法、知识体系与学科。

abstract.en: To know is the heart of science.
abstract.cn: 「知道」是 science 的核心。

examples.en: Science has changed daily life.
examples.cn: 科学改变了日常生活。

examples.en: She studies computer science.
examples.cn: 她学习计算机科学。

examples.en: The science of medicine grows fast.
examples.cn: 医学科学发展得很快。

dict_mnemonic.text: science 源自拉丁语 scire（知道），ence 构成名词，所以 science 就是「系统化的知识」。

root: 源自拉丁语 scientia（知识），来自 scire（知道），核心义「经系统研究获得的知识」。

sensesIntro.en: Science means systematic knowledge, the activity of research, or a particular field of study.
sensesIntro.cn: science 意为系统知识、研究活动，或某个学科。

core.en: Knowledge built by observation and testing.
core.cn: 通过观察与检验建立的知识。

branches.en: Organized knowledge of nature.
branches.cn: 关于自然的有组织知识。

branches.en: The work of testing and discovering.
One named branch such as chemistry.
branches.cn: 像化学这样的具体学科。

branches.en: Knowledge and research depend on each other.
Each discipline has its own methods.
branches.cn: 每个学科都有自己的方法。

intro.en: Science forms words for its method, people, and fields.
intro.cn: science 构成表示方法、人物与学科的词汇。

latinIntro.en: Latin scientia and scire are the sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scientia 与 scire 是词源。

科学家们分享研究结果。

计算机科学吸引许多学生。

items.meaning: the study of people and society

definition_en: to touch something quickly and with force, or to reach a target
core_image: 球棒与球接触的那一瞬间
scene: 棒球课上教练纠正挥棒姿势后，小选手一棒把球打出场外围栏。 He swung hard and hit the incoming pitch out of the park.
sceneCN: 这里 hit 是「击打；击中」（第 1 个义项：用力快速接触）；句中挥棒正中来球，球飞出场外，正是 hit 的动作。

derivatives.zh: 现在分词，义为「击打（进行中）」
动词加名词后缀构成，义为「击球手」
复合词，义为「职业杀手」
复数名词，义为「热门作品；点击量」

senses.title: To strike with force
senses.definition: to touch someone or something quickly and with force
senses.definitionCN: 快速而用力地接触人或物
senses.example: The batsman hit the ball towards the river.
senses.exampleCN: 击球手把球朝河边打了出去。
senses.why: Speed plus force in one touch is the heart of striking.
senses.whyCN: 快速与用力一次完成，就是击打的核心。

senses.title: To crash into something
senses.definition: to crash into something with force
senses.definitionCN: 用力撞上某物
senses.example: The truck hit a tree near the bend.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车在弯道附近撞上了一棵树。
senses.why: A moving body that cannot stop strikes whatever is ahead.
senses.whyCN: 停不下来的运动物体会撞上前方的任何东西。

senses.title: To reach a level or number
senses.definition: to reach a particular level, number, or price
senses.definitionCN: 达到某个数量、水平或价格
senses.example: The video hit one million views overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 视频一夜之间达到一百万播放量。
senses.why: A rising number arrives at its target like a fist at a mark.
senses.whyCN: 上升的数字像拳头一样「命中」目标刻度。

senses.title: A popular success
senses.definition: a thing, song, or show that becomes very popular
senses.definitionCN: 大受欢迎的歌曲、作品或演出
senses.example: Her first song was an instant hit online.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一首歌在网上迅速走红。
senses.why: What strikes the audience lands deep, so success is a hit.
senses.whyCN: 击中观众内心的作品，就叫 hit。

intro.en: Hit is a short native word with a violent history.
intro.cn: hit 是个简短的本族词，来历与打击相关。

items.en: Old English hittan meant to come upon or to meet by chance.
items.cn: 古英语 hittan 意为偶然遇到、碰上。

items.en: It was likely borrowed from Old Norse hitta, to hit upon or find.
items.cn: 它可能借自古诺斯语 hitta，意为碰上、找到。

items.en: The root belongs to the Germanic family of meeting and striking.
items.cn: 词根属日耳曼语族，兼有「相遇」与「击打」之意。

items.en: Middle English narrowed the sense to striking with a weapon or hand.
items.cn: 中古英语词义收窄为用手或武器击打。

items.en: Modern English added senses of reaching numbers and of popular success.
items.cn: 现代英语又添加了「达到数字」与「热门作品」之义。

note.en: Compare hit with its forms and near words.
note.cn: 把 hit 与其词形及近义词对照。

entries.definition: present participle with doubled t
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，双写 t

entries.definition: a player who hits
entries.definitionCN: 击球手，派生名词

entries.definition: warmth, a different word
entries.definitionCN: 热量，元音不同，词源无关

entries.definition: to hit forcefully, often once
entries.definitionCN: 用力击打，常指一次重击

entries.definition: to hit a door or surface to get attention
entries.definitionCN: 敲击以引起注意

entries.definition: to break by hitting hard
entries.definitionCN: 猛击并打碎，程度更强

normalIntro.en: Keep hit in motion scenes.
normalIntro.cn: 把 hit 放在运动场景中记忆。

normal.en: hit never changes: hit, hit, hit.
normal.cn: hit 的过去式、过去分词不变：hit, hit, hit。

normal.en: Only the -ing doubles the t: hitting.
normal.cn: 只有进行时分词双写 t：hitting。

normal.en: hit the road means start your journey.
normal.cn: hit the road 意为「出发上路」，与打无关。

normal.en: A hit song strikes the heart of millions.
normal.cn: hit song 击中了百万人的心——热门就是这么来的。

normal.en: Views can hit a number, like an arrow at a target.
normal.cn: 播放量能 hit 一个数字，如箭中靶。

abstract.en: Hear the sharp crack of bat on ball.
abstract.cn: 听见球棒击球的脆响——hit 的声音。

abstract.en: Feel the shock travel up your arm.
abstract.cn: 感受冲击顺着手臂传上来——hit 的触感。

abstract.en: See the number climb and touch the record line.
abstract.cn: 看见数字爬升触到纪录线——hit 的量感。

examples.en: Do not hit the dog; shout to warn it instead.
examples.cn: 别打狗，用喊声提醒它。

examples.en: The car hit the wall at the end of the street.
examples.cn: 汽车在街尾撞上了墙。

examples.en: The new phone hit the market last week.
examples.cn: 新手机上周上市了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嘿特」——「嘿，特准一击命中」，出手快狠正是 hit。

root: hit 大概率借自古诺斯语 hitta（碰上、找到），古英语 hittan（偶然遇到）与之呼应，属日耳曼语族；中古英语词义收窄为「击打」，现代英语再扩展出「达到」与「热门」之义。

sensesIntro.en: From a single blow to a record number to a hit song, one contact grows into many ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: hit 从一次击打延伸到「达到数值」「热门作品」，一切围绕「接触与命中」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the instant of fast, forceful contact
core.cn: 核心意象：快速而有力的接触瞬间

branches.en: a blow with hand or tool
a crash between moving things
branches.cn: 运动物体间的碰撞（义项 02）

branches.en: arriving at a number or level
branches.cn: 达到某个数字或水平（义项 03）

branches.en: a work that strikes the public
force meeting a surface

intro.cn: hit 构成与冲击、成功相关的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin percutere covers striking in scientific words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 percutere 在科学词汇中表示击打。

definition_en: the woman a man or woman is married to, seen from the partner s side
core_image: 两只并排挂在门边的结婚戒指照片，框里两个人肩膀挨得很近
scene: 他指着厨房里那位系着围裙的人，说这就是他妻子，然后笑着去洗碗。 His wife teaches at the school at the end of our street.
sceneCN: 这里 wife 是「妻子」（第 1 个义项：与之结婚的那位女性，从配偶一方来看）；句意为他妻子在我们街尾那所学校教书。门边并排挂着的合照，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 妻子（复数）
家庭主妇
助产士
（旧）妻子般的

senses.title: The married partner
senses.definition: the woman to whom a person is married, spoken of from the other partner s side
senses.definitionCN: 一个人与之结婚的女性，从配偶另一方的角度来说
senses.example: His wife teaches at the school at the end of our street.
senses.exampleCN: 他妻子在我们街尾那所学校教书。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense, a role named from the viewpoint of the person married to her.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常意义，是从与她结婚之人的视角命名的一个角色。

senses.title: A woman in old use
senses.definition: in older English, any adult woman, without any link to marriage
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的英语中泛指成年女性，与婚姻无关
senses.example: In Middle English a wife could mean simply a woman of any rank.
senses.exampleCN: 在中古英语里，wife 可以单纯指任何身份的女性。
senses.why: The broad sense is the original one, and it survives today only inside fixed compounds.
senses.whyCN: 这个宽泛的意义才是最初的义项，今天只在固定复合词内部存活。

senses.title: In fixed pairs
senses.definition: used in paired phrases such as husband and wife or man and wife
senses.definitionCN: 用于 husband and wife、man and wife 这类成对说法
senses.example: They were pronounced man and wife before the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在全村人面前被宣布为夫妻。
senses.why: The wedding formula keeps the older style, and the pair sounds like one unit.
senses.whyCN: 婚礼套语保留了更古老的说法，这一对词听起来像一个整体。

senses.title: Inside compounds
senses.definition: used as a second element in words such as housewife and midwife
senses.definitionCN: 作为 housewife、midwife 等词的后项出现
senses.example: His mother had been a housewife for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他母亲做了三十年家庭主妇。
senses.why: Old compounds kept the broad sense of woman, which is why a midwife is not simply a married woman.
senses.whyCN: 古老的复合词保留了「女性」的宽泛意义，所以 midwife 并不只是已婚妇女。

senses.title: In respectful address
senses.definition: in older formal usage, a title for a married woman, often written before her family name
senses.definitionCN: 在旧式正式用法中，作为已婚女性的称谓，常写在姓氏之前
senses.example: The letter began with a greeting to the doctor and his wife.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信开头向医生和他的夫人问候。
senses.why: The title dropped out of most modern use, and the plain noun is now the neutral choice.
senses.whyCN: 这一称谓在现代多数用法中已消失，普通名词成为中性选择。

intro.en: Wife comes from Old English wif, which meant woman in general, not a married one; the narrowing to married partner came later.
intro.cn: wife 源自古英语 wif，本泛指女性而非已婚者，限定为配偶的意义是后来才出现的。

items.en: The root meant woman, and the related word for a male partner was separate.
items.cn: 这个词根意为女性，指男性配偶的词则另有一个。

items.en: Wif meant woman, and wifman and wermann paired a woman and a man as humans.
items.cn: wif 指女性，wifman 与 wermann 则以「人」为后项来指男女。

items.en: Wif narrowed towards married woman, while woman took over the general sense.
items.cn: wif 的词义收窄为已婚女性，泛指的意义由 woman 接手。

items.en: The plural wives kept the old f to v change, the only trace of the older grammar.
items.cn: 复数 wives 保留了 f 变 v 的变化，这是旧语法的唯一痕迹。

items.en: Compounds such as housewife and midwife still carry the older sense of woman.
items.cn: housewife 与 midwife 这类复合词仍带着旧有的「女性」之义。

note.en: The first group gathers the marriage and family words that look close, the second the words for a partner in general.
note.cn: 第一组收形近的婚姻与家庭词，第二组收泛指伴侣的词。

entries.definition: The male partner in the same relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 丈夫

entries.definition: The plural, with f turned to v.
entries.definitionCN: 妻子们

entries.definition: The state of being alive, one letter apart.
entries.definitionCN: 生命；生活

entries.definition: A cutting tool, the same f sound.
entries.definitionCN: 刀子

entries.definition: A partner in marriage, of either sex.
entries.definitionCN: 配偶

entries.definition: The person one lives with or shares life with.
entries.definitionCN: 伴侣；搭档

entries.definition: A woman on her wedding day.
entries.definitionCN: 新娘

normalIntro.en: Wife has only one irregular point, the plural wives, and one surprising fact, that it once meant woman.
normalIntro.cn: wife 只有一个不规则点，即复数 wives，还有一个意外事实：它原本指「女性」。

normal.en: Wife turns to wives, and so do knife and life.
normal.cn: wife 变 wives，knife 和 life 也一样。

normal.en: Husband and wife is a fixed pair that reads like one word.
normal.cn: husband and wife 是固定一对，读起来像一个词。

normal.en: A midwife helps at births because the old word meant a woman.
normal.cn: midwife 负责接生，因为旧义就是「女性」。

normal.en: The -fe ending is the only sign of the old grammar left.
normal.cn: 这个 -fe 词尾是旧语法留下的唯一迹象。

normal.en: Remember it as a role seen from the partner s side.
normal.cn: 把它记作从配偶那一侧看到的角色。

abstract.en: See two rings hanging side by side by a door.
abstract.cn: 看见两枚戒指并排挂在门边。

abstract.en: Hear a name introduced with one word in front of it.
abstract.cn: 听一个名字前面只加了一个词就被介绍出来。

abstract.en: Feel a shoulder close to another shoulder in an old photo.
abstract.cn: 感觉老照片里一个肩膀紧挨着另一个肩膀。

examples.en: He and his wife have lived here for forty years.
examples.cn: 他和妻子在这里住了四十年。

examples.en: The two of them were man and wife by the end of the day.
examples.cn: 一天结束的时候，他们俩成了夫妻。

examples.en: The old house belonged to the doctor and his wife.
examples.cn: 那所老房子属于医生和他夫人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「怀福」——怀里揣着福气的人，就是妻子。

root: 日耳曼语词根（女性）→ 古英语 wif（女人）→ 中古英语 wif（妻子）→ 现代英语 wife；同族有 wives、housewife、midwife。

sensesIntro.en: The word began as woman, narrowed to the married partner, settled in wedding formulas, lived on inside compounds, and faded as a title of address.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词原本指女性，收窄为配偶，固定在婚礼套语里，存活于复合词内部，最后作为称谓逐渐淡出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rings hanging side by side by the same door.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一扇门边并排挂着的两枚戒指。

branches.en: The everyday branch: a teacher at the end of the street.
branches.cn: 日常分支：街尾教书的妻子。

branches.en: The old branch: any woman of any rank.
branches.cn: 旧义分支：任何身份的女性。

branches.en: The wedding branch: pronounced man and wife.
branches.cn: 婚礼分支：被宣布为夫妻。

branches.en: The compound branch: thirty years as a housewife.
branches.cn: 复合词分支：三十年家庭主妇。

branches.en: The title branch: a letter to the doctor and his wife.
branches.cn: 称谓分支：写给医生夫妇的信。

intro.en: Wife is a root noun whose plural is irregular, and it survives inside old compounds where the second place was once open to any word for woman.
intro.cn: wife 是复数不规则的词根名词，它在古老的复合词中仍然存活，那些复合词的后项原本可换成任何表示女性的词。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below give the borrowed words that translate it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目给出用来翻译它的借入词。

items.example: It gives midwife, a woman who helps at birth.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 midwife，即接生的女性。

items.example: The wedding formula of the old style.
The pair reads as one unit.
items.exampleCN: 这一对读来像一个整体。

latinEntries.example: It shows the older broad sense side by side.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它与更宽泛的旧义并立。

definition_zh: 附近的；邻近的；在附近；就近
definition_en: a short distance away from the place being talked about, used either before a noun or after a verb
core_image: 两户人家的院墙只隔一条窄巷，站在门口就能看见对方窗里的灯
scene: 傍晚的巷口，两棵梧桐树下摆着几张矮桌，邻居端着碗坐在门口。 A nearby shop was still open, and the children ran in for sweets.
sceneCN: 这里是「附近的」（第 1 个义项：作形容词，指距离不远）；句意为附近那家小店还开着，孩子们跑进去买糖。图中可辨识物件：巷口、梧桐、矮桌、饭碗。

derivatives.zh: nearby 的构词来源，义为「近的；接近的」
与 nearby 同出 near，加 -ly 后义为「几乎」
由 near 加 -ness 构成，义为「接近；临近」

senses.title: Close to the place mentioned, before a noun
senses.definition: used before a noun for a place or thing that is only a short distance from the place being talked about
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词之前，指距离所说地点不远的地方或事物
senses.example: A nearby shop was still open, and the children ran in for sweets.
senses.exampleCN: 附近一家小店还开着，孩子们跑进去买糖。
senses.why: Near came from Old English neah, close at hand, and by from Old English bi, beside; putting them together produced a word whose whole job is to sit in front of a place and shorten the distance.
senses.whyCN: near 来自古英语 neah，意为「在手边」；by 来自古英语 bi，意为「在旁边」；两者合起来，造出一个专门放在地点名词前、把距离缩短的词。

senses.title: At a short distance away, after a verb
senses.definition: used after a verb or at the end of a clause to say that something happens a short distance from the place mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 放在动词之后或句末，表示事情发生在离所说地点不远的地方
senses.example: She lives nearby and walks over most mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 她住在附近，大多数早晨都走过来。
senses.why: English often lets a compound work as an adverb without any ending, so the same two prepositions that named a place beside another place also came to describe where an action happens.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让一个复合词不带词尾就直接作副词，于是原本用来说「在一个地点旁边的另一个地点」的两个介词，也用来描述动作发生在哪里。

intro.en: Nearby is a plain English compound of two Old English words for closeness, and it has been recorded only since the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: nearby 是两个表示「接近」的古英语词合成的普通英语复合词，有记录的历史只能追溯到十八世纪。

items.en: Neah meant close at hand, and its comparative near later became an ordinary adjective for what is not far.
items.cn: neah 意为在手边，它的比较级 near 后来变成普通形容词，表示「不远的」。

items.en: Bi meant beside, near or by the side of, and it survives in by, beside and the second half of nearby.
items.cn: bi 意为在旁边、靠近，它留在 by、beside 以及 nearby 的后半截里。

items.en: Middle English already paired near with by in phrases about standing or living close to a place.
items.cn: 中古英语已在表示「站在或住在某处近旁」的短语里把 near 与 by 配在一起。

items.en: The written compound nearby appears in the eighteenth century, first in American usage, and spreads in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 写成一个词的 nearby 在十八世纪出现，最早见于美国用法，十九世纪渐渐流行。

items.en: Modern English uses it both before nouns and after verbs, so one form covers two grammatical jobs.
items.cn: 现代英语让它既用于名词之前，也用于动词之后，同一个形式承担两种语法角色。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the two words that were joined to make the compound plus their derived forms; the near-meaning group holds adjectives and adverbs of closeness.
note.cn: 形近组收合成这个复合词的两个来源词及其派生形式；近义组收表示「接近」的形容词与副词。

entries.definition: Not far away, as a preposition, adjective or adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 不远的；作介词、形容词或副词。

entries.definition: Almost, but not quite; built on the same root with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎但不完全；同一词根加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being close in space or time.
entries.definitionCN: 空间或时间上接近的状态。

entries.definition: The superlative of near, for the shortest distance of all.
entries.definitionCN: near 的最高级，表示距离最短。

entries.definition: Only a small distance away, often with a stronger sense of contact.
entries.definitionCN: 距离很小，常带「贴近」的意味。

entries.definition: Lying next to something, usually sharing a border.
entries.definitionCN: 紧挨着某物，通常指相邻接壤。

entries.definition: Situated next to or in the same district as something else.
entries.definitionCN: 位于某物旁边或同一区域的。

entries.definition: In the area on every side of a place, without naming one spot.
entries.definitionCN: 在某地四周的范围内，不指某一处。

normalIntro.en: The word is simply near plus by, two old English words for closeness that fused into one adjective and adverb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 near 加 by，两个表示「接近」的古英语词合并成一个形容词兼副词。

normal.en: Old English neah meant close at hand, and by came from bi, beside; nearby is those two ideas welded together.
normal.cn: 古英语 neah 意为在手边，by 来自 bi（在旁边）；nearby 就是这两个意思焊在一起。

normal.en: The compound is written as one word, unlike the phrase near by, which still appears in older texts.
normal.cn: 这个复合词写成一个词，与旧文献里仍能见到的短语 near by 不同。

normal.en: Before a noun it is an adjective: a nearby town; after a verb it is an adverb: she lives nearby.
normal.cn: 放在名词前是形容词：a nearby town；放在动词后是副词：she lives nearby。

normal.en: Nearly looks like the same word with -ly, but it means almost, not at a short distance.
normal.cn: nearly 看起来只是加了 -ly，意思却是「几乎」，而不是「在不远处」。

normal.en: Nearness is the noun made with -ness, useful when the sentence needs a subject rather than a place.
normal.cn: nearness 是用 -ness 构成的名词，句子需要一个主语而不是地点时就用它。

abstract.en: Two short words for standing beside something can do the work of a whole phrase about distance.
abstract.cn: 两个表示「站在旁边」的短词，就能顶替一整句关于距离的描述。

abstract.en: A word that only shortens distance shows how much English trusts a compound to do a preposition's job.
abstract.cn: 一个只负责缩短距离的词，说明英语多么信任复合词去承担介词的工作。

abstract.en: What is nearby is not yet reached, which is why the word always leaves a small gap open.
abstract.cn: 「附近的」东西还没有被走到，所以这个词总留着一小段没走完的距离。

examples.en: Several nearby farms lost power in the storm.
examples.cn: 附近几座农场在风暴中停了电。

examples.en: The hotel is convenient for nearby restaurants.
examples.cn: 这家旅馆去附近的餐馆很方便。

examples.en: My parents live nearby, so we see them often.
examples.cn: 我父母住在附近，所以我们常去看他们。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼尔拜」——抬脚就到旁边那条街，说一声就到了；nearby 就是附近的。

root: 古英语 neah（近）与 bi（在旁）复合，十八世纪出现 nearby；属日耳曼语词，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place at a short distance; the same form then splits by grammar into an adjective in front of nouns and an adverb after verbs.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「距离不远的一处地方」；同一个形式随后按语法分工，成了名词前的形容词和动词后的副词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two garden walls separated by a narrow lane, each house able to see the other's lamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：两户院墙之间只隔一条窄巷，各家都能看见对方窗里的灯。

branches.en: a shop two doors down the lane
branches.cn: 隔两个门面的那家小店

branches.en: a village within walking distance
a lane where both walls can see one lamp
branches.cn: 两面墙都看得见同一盏灯的窄巷

branches.en: a neighbour walking over with a bowl
branches.cn: 端着一只碗走过来的邻居

branches.en: a short walk taken most mornings
branches.cn: 大多数早晨都要走的一小段路

intro.en: The word is built from an Old English adjective of closeness, an Old English preposition of position, and the English endings that grew around them.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语中表示「接近」的形容词、表示位置的介词，以及围着它们长出的英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Near and by are Germanic words, and no reliable Latin cognate is recorded for the compound.
latinIntro.cn: near 与 by 都是日耳曼语词，这个复合词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_en: the child of one's son or daughter
core_image: 隔一代的孩子：你孩子的小孩，坐你膝头喊爷爷奶奶
scene: 老人翻出旧相册，指着一张满月照。 Her youngest grandchild was born last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 grandchild 是「孙辈」（第 1 个义项：子女的孩子）；句意为她最小的孙辈去年春天出生。

pos.zh: 名词：孙子；孙女；孙辈（不分男女）

derivatives.zh: 同一 grand- 家族，指孙女
同一 grand- 家族，指孙子
同一 grand- 家族，指祖父母或外祖父母

senses.title: A child of your child
senses.definition: a son or daughter of your own son or daughter
senses.definitionCN: 你儿子或你女儿的孩子
senses.example: Each grandchild got a red envelope at New Year.
senses.exampleCN: 每个孙辈过年都收到一个红包。
senses.why: The core image is one generation of distance: child of my child.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是隔一代的血缘：我孩子的孩子。

senses.title: A cherished youngest member
senses.definition: any young relative treated with special fondness, loosely used
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛地指被特别疼爱的幼小亲属
senses.example: The whole village treats the boy as a grandchild.
senses.exampleCN: 全村人都把那男孩当自家孙辈疼。
senses.why: Warm family feeling extends the kinship term to beloved young outsiders.
senses.whyCN: 家庭的温情把亲属称谓推及到受疼爱的幼小外人，义项随之放宽。

intro.en: Grandchild joins the French-born grand- with the Old English child.
intro.cn: grandchild 把法语出身的 grand- 接到古英语 child 上。

items.en: Old French grand meant large or great, used in family terms.
items.cn: 古法语 grand 意为大、great，用于家庭称谓。

items.en: Latin grandis meant large, fully grown.
items.cn: 拉丁语 grandis 意为大的、成年的。

items.en: English borrowed grand- into kinship words like grandchild.
items.cn: 中古英语把 grand- 借入亲属称谓，如 grandchild。

items.en: The plural grandchildren follows the irregular plural of child.
items.cn: 现代英语中复数 grandchildren 沿用 child 的不规则复数。

items.en: Modern English uses grandchild across the grand- family.
items.cn: 现代英语中 grandchild 与 grand- 词族并用。

note.en: The grand- family covers two generations at once.
note.cn: grand- 家族一次覆盖两代亲属。

entries.definition: the plural of grandchild
entries.definitionCN: grandchild 的复数

entries.definition: a rare descriptive coinage, not standard
entries.definitionCN: 少见派生拼法，并非标准词

entries.definition: an uncle of one's parent; same grand- prefix
entries.definitionCN: 父母的叔伯；共用 grand- 前缀

entries.definition: a female grandchild
entries.definitionCN: 孙女，特指女性孙辈

entries.definition: a male grandchild
entries.definitionCN: 孙子，特指男性孙辈

entries.definition: any later-generation relative
entries.definitionCN: 后代，泛指更晚的世代

normalIntro.en: Five hooks for the youngest branch of the family tree.
normalIntro.cn: 家族树上最嫩一枝的五条钩子。

normal.en: Grand means one step big: your child's child.
normal.cn: grand 表示「大一步」：你孩子的孩子。

normal.en: Grandchildren keep the irregular plural of child.
normal.cn: grandchildren 保留 child 的不规则复数。

normal.en: Grandparents often spoil their grandchildren.
normal.cn: 祖辈常溺爱孙辈。

normal.en: Grand + child is grandparent's mirror word.
normal.cn: grand + child 是 grandparent 的镜像词。

normal.en: Family photos pass from grandchild to grandchild.
normal.cn: 家庭相册在孙辈之间传递。

abstract.en: A grandchild is your second spring.
abstract.cn: 孙辈是你的第二个春天。

abstract.en: The family tree grows a new ring.
abstract.cn: 家族之树长出一圈新轮。

abstract.en: Two hands apart, one heart between: grandparent and grandchild.
abstract.cn: 隔两只手，共一颗心：祖辈与孙辈。

examples.en: My eldest grandchild starts school this autumn.
examples.cn: 我最大的孙辈今年秋天上学。

examples.en: Grandparents tell stories to their grandchildren.
examples.cn: 祖辈给孙辈们讲故事。

examples.en: She hopes to see each grandchild grow up healthy.
examples.cn: 她希望看着每个孙辈健康长大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歌兰猜得」——隔一代的血缘要靠家谱去猜数；grandchild 就是隔代的孩子

root: 法语 grand（拉丁语 grandis「大」）作前缀表示隔一代 + 古英语 child（孩子）；复合词，复数沿用 child→children。

sensesIntro.en: A single kinship sense: the child of one's own child.
sensesIntro.cn: 单一亲属义项：自己孩子的孩子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the child standing one generation away
core.cn: 核心意象：隔一代站立的孩子

branches.en: child of my child
the treasured youngest member
the mirror of grandparent
the link across generations
the new ring on the tree

intro.en: Grand- is the workhorse prefix of English kinship terms.
intro.cn: grand- 是英语亲属称谓的主力前缀。

latinIntro.en: The prefix goes back to Latin grandis, meaning large.
latinIntro.cn: 该前缀源自拉丁语 grandis，意为大。

items.example: Grand- builds grandfather and grandchild alike.
Child is the core of the compound.

items.exampleCN: 那里挂着曾孙辈的照片。
周末是孙辈来访的日子。

items.example: The grand- family spans two generations.

definition_zh: 管理；掌管；设法做到；勉力完成；应付；对付；靠有限的收入过日子
definition_en: to be in charge of a business or team, to succeed in doing something difficult, to deal with a hard person or situation, or to live on limited means
core_image: 一只手把缰绳一点点收短，躁动的马被稳稳按住
scene: 清晨的马场里，驯马师把缰绳一点点收短，躁动的马终于站定。 By evening she was managing the whole stable on her own.
sceneCN: 这里 manage 是「管理、掌管」（第 1 个义项：对一批事务负起责任并决定它如何运转）；句意为到傍晚时，她一个人管着整座马房。图中可辨识物件：收短的缰绳、被按住的马、木栏与草料桶。

pos.zh: 管理；掌管；设法做到；应付；靠有限的钱维持

derivatives.zh: 由 manage 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「管理者；经理」
由 manage 加表示「行为、结果」的后缀 -ment 构成，义为「管理；管理层」
由 manage 加表示「可以……的」后缀 -able 构成，义为「可控制的；对付得了的」
由 manager 加 -ial 构成，义为「管理层的；经营上的」

senses.title: To be in charge of a business or team
senses.definition: to have responsibility for a company, a team or a set of affairs and decide how it should be run
senses.definitionCN: 对一家公司、一支团队或一批事务负起责任，并决定它该如何运转
senses.example: She manages a small team of six engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 她管理着一个由六名工程师组成的小团队。
senses.why: Italian maneggiare first meant to handle a horse with your hands, so the grip on the reins became the grip on a business: control is felt as something held, not merely ordered.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 maneggiare 最初指用手去摆弄、驯服一匹马，于是握住缰绳的那只手后来握住了事务：所谓控制，是被握住的感觉，而不只是发号施令。

senses.title: To succeed in doing something difficult
senses.definition: to succeed in doing something, especially when serious difficulties stand in the way
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在明显阻碍之下，仍然把某事做成
senses.example: He managed to finish the report before the power failed.
senses.exampleCN: 他赶在断电之前设法把报告写完了。
senses.why: A handler gets a stubborn animal to move by working it patiently, step after step; the word for handling therefore also means pushing a hard task through to the end.
senses.whyCN: 驯手对付一头犟牲口，是一步又一步耐心摆弄着让它动起来；所以「摆弄」这个词也用来表示把一件难事一路推到做成。

senses.title: To cope with a difficult person or situation
senses.definition: to deal with a difficult person, feeling or situation without losing control of it
senses.definitionCN: 面对难缠的人、情绪或局面，仍能不失控地应对下去
senses.example: She manages difficult customers without ever raising her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她应付难缠的顾客时从不提高嗓门。
senses.why: If managing is keeping a firm hand on something, a difficult customer is only one more thing that must be held steady instead of dropped.
senses.whyCN: 既然管理就是把一件东西稳稳握在手里，那么难缠的顾客也不过是另一件必须稳住、不能松手的东西。

senses.title: To live on limited money or time
senses.titleCN: 靠有限的收入过日子；精打细算
senses.definition: to live or keep going with only a small amount of money or time, using it carefully
senses.definitionCN: 在钱或时间很少的情况下，仔细盘算着维持下去
senses.example: The family manages on one small pension.
senses.exampleCN: 这一家人靠一份微薄的养老金过日子。
senses.why: Running a household on little money is the same skill of handling resources, so manage also came to mean stretching whatever is already in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 用很少的钱撑起一个家，仍是同一套摆弄资源的本事，于是 manage 又表示把手里已经有的那点东西拉长来用。

intro.en: Manage reaches English through Italian and French, and the word still smells of the stable: to manage a horse came before managing a company.
intro.cn: manage 经意大利语与法语进入英语，词里至今还留着马房的气味：先会驯马，后来才谈管理公司。

items.en: Manus is the ordinary Latin noun for the hand, and the hand was the ancient image of control over any object.
items.cn: manus 是拉丁语中表示「手」的普通名词，而手一向是「掌控某物」的古老形象。

items.en: Italian kept the Latin noun as mano, still meaning hand, and built its verb of handling on that base.
items.cn: 意大利语把拉丁名词保留为 mano，仍指手，并在这个词基上造出了表示「摆弄」的动词。

items.en: Maneggiare meant to work something with the hands, above all to train and ride a horse in the riding school.
items.cn: maneggiare 意为用手去弄某样东西，其中最主要指在马术学校里驯马、驭马。

items.en: French manège named a riding school and the art taught there; its form and its stable sense pressed on the English borrowing of the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 manège 指马术学校以及在那里教的技艺；它的词形与马房义在十六世纪影响了英语的借入形式。

items.en: Modern English drops the stable and keeps the grip, managing ships, money, staff, crowds and finally a difficult afternoon.
items.cn: 现代英语丢掉了马房，只留下那只握住的手，用它来管船、管钱、管人、管人群，最后也管一个难熬的下午。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers derivatives and words built on the Latin noun for hand; the near group gathers verbs for running, handling and coping.
note.cn: 形近组收派生词以及建立在拉丁语「手」这个名词上的词；近义组收表示经营、处理与应对的动词。

entries.definition: The person who manages a team or a business.
entries.definitionCN: 管理团队或业务的人；由 manage 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The activity of managing, or the people who run a firm.
entries.definitionCN: 管理这项活动；也指经营一家公司的那批人；由 manage 加 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: Easy enough to control or deal with.
entries.definitionCN: 容易控制或应付的；由 manage 加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: Done with the hands, or a handbook of instructions; from Latin manus, hand.
entries.definitionCN: 用手做的；也指操作手册；出自拉丁语 manus（手），与 manage 同源。

entries.definition: To handle or control something, often by unfair means.
entries.definitionCN: 摆弄或操控某物，常指用不正当手段；词根同为拉丁语 manus（手）。

entries.definition: To be in charge of and operate a business or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 负责经营一家企业或机构。

entries.definition: To work or control a machine, a system or a business.
entries.definitionCN: 操作机器、系统，或经营业务。

entries.definition: To deal with a person, a problem or a situation.
entries.definitionCN: 应付某人、某个问题或某种局面。

entries.definition: To deal successfully with a difficult situation.
entries.definitionCN: 成功应对困难的局面。

entries.definition: To watch over people or work and make sure it is done properly.
entries.definitionCN: 监督人或工作，确保其正常进行。

normalIntro.en: The word grew out of a stable, where managing meant working the reins with your hands, and its family keeps returning to grip, affairs and tasks pushed through.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从马房里长出来，那时的 manage 是用手摆弄缰绳；它的同族词反复回到握持、事务，以及被推到做成的难事。

normal.en: Latin manus means hand, and Italian made maneggiare from mano, so to manage is first to have something in your hand.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 manus 意为手，意大利语又用 mano 造出 maneggiare，所以 manage 起初就是把某样东西握在手里。

normal.en: The earliest English sense is to train a horse, which is why a rider's control still sits inside the modern word.
normal.cn: 这个词在英语里最早的意思是驯马，所以骑手那种控制感至今还留在现代词义里。

normal.en: French manège, a riding school, reshaped the borrowed word in the sixteenth century and kept the stable flavour.
normal.cn: 法语 manège 指马术学校，它在十六世纪改塑了这个借词，也留下了马房的气息。

normal.en: Manager adds -er for the person, management adds -ment for the activity, manageable adds -able for what can be handled.
normal.cn: manager 加 -er 指人，management 加 -ment 指活动，manageable 加 -able 指「拿得住、对付得了」。

normal.en: Manage to do keeps the old image: you work the task with your hands until it finally moves.
normal.cn: manage to do 保留着旧画面：你用双手反复摆弄那件事，直到它终于动起来。

abstract.en: Control is pictured as a grip: what you cannot hold, you cannot manage.
abstract.cn: 控制被想象成一次握持：握不住的东西，就管不了。

abstract.en: A horse, a company and a bad afternoon are all things the same hand is asked to steady.
abstract.cn: 一匹马、一家公司、一个难熬的下午，都是同一只手被要求稳住的东西。

abstract.en: The word began in a stable and ended in an office, yet the gesture never changed.
abstract.cn: 这个词起于马房，落于办公室，中间的那个动作却始终没变。

examples.en: She manages a small team of six engineers.
examples.cn: 她管理着一个由六名工程师组成的小团队。

examples.en: He managed to finish the report before the power failed.
examples.cn: 他赶在断电之前设法把报告写完了。

examples.en: The family manages on one small pension.
examples.cn: 这一家人靠一份微薄的养老金过日子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马那吉」——马那吉一手拉住缰绳，烈马就听话了；记住 manage 是驾驭、管理，也是设法做到。

root: 意大利语 maneggiare（用手摆弄、驯马）出自 mano（手），再上溯到拉丁语 manus（手）；英语在十六世纪借入 manage，并受法语 manège（马术学校）影响。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a hand keeping a grip on something; the senses then divide into running affairs, forcing a hard task through, steadying difficult people, and stretching scarce means.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一只手把某样东西握稳；义项由此分成掌管事务、把难事推到做成、稳住难缠的人，以及把不多的资源拉长来用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand shortening the reins until a restless horse stands still.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把缰绳收短，直到躁动的马站定不动。

branches.en: a hand tightening the reins in a stable yard
branches.cn: 马场里一只手收紧缰绳

branches.en: a manager calming an angry customer at the counter
branches.cn: 管理者在柜台前安抚愤怒的顾客

branches.en: a report finished one minute before the power cut
branches.cn: 报告在断电前一分钟写完

branches.en: a queue kept in order through a busy afternoon
branches.cn: 队伍在繁忙的午后被维持住秩序

branches.en: one pension stretched across a whole month
branches.cn: 一份养老金撑过整整一个月

intro.en: The Latin noun for hand, its Italian and French descendants, the English verb and three English endings carry manage from a horse's reins to an office desk.
intro.cn: 拉丁语里表示「手」的名词、它的意大利语与法语后代、英语动词本身，再加三个英语词尾，把 manage 从马缰带到办公桌。

latinIntro.en: Latin manus, hand, is the reliable source of the family; the verb came to English through Italian maneggiare, with French manège shaping its later use.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 manus（手）是这个词族可靠的源头；动词经意大利语 maneggiare 进入英语，法语 manège 又影响了它后来的用法。

items.meaning: to handle, to train a horse

definition_en: a printed paper form telling a bank to pay money from your account (British spelling)
core_image: 一张从支票簿撕下的付款单，交给银行就能换钱
scene: 爸爸把填好的支票交给学校财务室的老师。 Dad paid the school fees by cheque.
sceneCN: 这里 cheque 是「支票」（第 1 个义项：向银行提款的单据）；句意为爸爸用支票交了学费。

derivatives.zh: 由 cheque 加 book 构成，义为「支票簿」
支票上的收款人（与 cheque 相关的银行用语）

senses.title: A paper order to a bank to pay money
senses.definition: a printed form that tells a bank to take money from your account and pay it to someone
senses.definitionCN: 通知银行从自己账户取款并支付给某人的印制单据
senses.example: Dad paid the school fees by cheque.
senses.exampleCN: 爸爸用支票交了学费。
senses.why: The bank 'checks' the order before paying: the examining call of chess became the paper of payment.
senses.whyCN: 银行付款前要「核验」指令：象棋的核验呼语便成了付款的单据。

senses.title: The bill for food or a service
senses.definition: the written bill in a restaurant (British use of the word check)
senses.definitionCN: 餐馆里的结账单（check 一词的英式用法）
senses.example: The waiter brought the cheque after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚餐后服务员送来账单。
senses.why: The bill is the paper on which you check what you owe before paying it.
senses.whyCN: 账单就是付钱前据以核对所欠款项的那张纸。

senses.title: Free permission to spend as much as wanted
senses.titleCN: 随意支配的许可（比喻用法）
senses.definition: complete freedom to use money or power, from the idea of a blank cheque
senses.definitionCN: 由空白支票引申的、不受限制使用金钱或权力的自由
senses.example: The coach was given a blank cheque to rebuild the team.
senses.exampleCN: 教练获得全权，放手重建球队。
senses.why: A blank cheque has no written amount, so it can name any permission without a limit.
senses.whyCN: 空白支票未写金额，便被借来指代没有限度的授权。

intro.en: Cheque is the British spelling of check, the chess word that became a bank paper.
intro.cn: cheque 是 check 的英式拼写，这个象棋词最终变成了银行单据。

items.en: Persian shah means king; in chess, calling shah freezes the king.
items.cn: 波斯语 shah 意为国王；棋局中喊 shah 可冻结王的行动。

items.en: Old French eschec carried the chess call and the sense of a rebuff.
items.cn: 古法语 eschec 承载棋语呼喊与挫败之义。

items.en: Middle English chek meant the chess call, a hindrance and a rebuke.
items.cn: 中古英语 chek 指棋语呼喊、阻碍与惩戒。

items.en: The bank paper called a check in America kept the older spelling.
items.cn: 这种银行单据在美国称 check，保留了较旧的拼写。

items.en: British English chose the French-style spelling cheque for the bank paper.
items.cn: 英式英语为该银行单据选择了法式拼写 cheque。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects payment words.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收付款类词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of cheque.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「支票」，是 cheque 的美式拼法。

entries.definition: A person who examines things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「检查员」，与 cheque 词首相同。

entries.definition: A stick for writing on boards.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「粉笔」，拼写与 cheque 相近。

entries.definition: A written demand for payment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「账单」，与 cheque 的账单义相近。

entries.definition: Money in coins or notes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「现金」，与支票同为付款方式。

entries.definition: A paper proving money was received.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收据」，付款后的凭证。

normalIntro.en: Remember cheque by its root and family.
normalIntro.cn: 借助词根与词族记忆 cheque。

normal.en: cheque is the British spelling of check.
normal.cn: cheque 是 check 的英式拼写。

normal.en: a chequebook holds all your cheques.
normal.cn: chequebook（支票簿）装着你的支票。

normal.en: a bounced cheque is one the bank refuses.
normal.cn: bounced cheque 指银行拒付的空头支票。

normal.en: a blank cheque also means unlimited freedom.
normal.cn: blank cheque 也喻指不受限制的授权。

normal.en: cash a cheque means to turn it into money.
normal.cn: cash a cheque 意为把支票兑换成现金。

abstract.en: Picture tearing one page from a small blue book.
abstract.cn: 想象从蓝色小本上撕下一页支票。

abstract.en: Hear the pen scratch a number into an empty box.
abstract.cn: 仿佛听见钢笔在空格里写下数字的沙沙声。

abstract.en: Feel the paper pass across the counter to the teller.
abstract.cn: 感受单据递过柜台的轻飘手感。

examples.en: Dad paid the school fees by cheque.
examples.cn: 爸爸用支票交了学费。

examples.en: The waiter brought the cheque after dinner.
examples.cn: 晚餐后服务员送来账单。

examples.en: She cashed a cheque at the bank counter.
examples.cn: 她在银行柜台兑现了一张支票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「切克」——切下一页支票交给银行核验。

root: 波斯语 shah（王）→ 古法语 eschec → 中古英语 chek → 现代英语 check / cheque；同根词有 checkmate（将死）、chess（国际象棋）、checker（检查员）。

sensesIntro.en: Cheque moves from a chess call to a bank paper, a restaurant bill and unlimited permission.
sensesIntro.cn: cheque 由象棋呼语到银行单据、餐馆账单与无限授权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a paper that orders the bank to pay
core.cn: 核心意象：一张命令银行付款的纸
